articles.title: Work with Action Center actions

sections.text: An action is one piece of work with an outcome, built from the evidence behind it. Ansvisor groups many signals into one action: six valuable pages with no AI traffic become one "Capture AI traffic" action with six linked signals, not six rows. New actions are added after the daily tracking run, on the **Actions** tab.

sections.heading: Action categories
sections.text:
- **Growth**: ground you could win, such as demand, topics, platforms or pages where you could appear more.
- **Protect**: ground you hold that is starting to slip.
- **Recover**: ground you held and lost, in visibility, citations, mentions or traffic.
- **Fix**: issues on your own site, such as low audit scores, blocked crawlers or broken links AI sends people to.
- **Compete**: places where competitors lead you.

sections.heading: Cards and filters
sections.text:
The cards at the top count and filter the list, all but **Highest Priority**. Click one to narrow the table, and click it again to clear it.

- **Top Actions**: the five highest-priority open actions.
- **At Risk**: open Recover and Fix actions.
- **Opportunities**: open Growth actions.
- **In Progress**: actions someone is working on.
- **Highest Priority**: the highest level among open actions; it doesn't filter. While Getting started runs, its card shows instead.

Below them, filter by category, **Priority**, **Status** and **Assignee**, or search. **Sort** by Priority (the default), Newest, Due date or Recently updated. Filters are kept in the page's address, so a filtered view can be shared. For an online shop, the **From Products** chip lists only the actions sent from Products.

sections.heading: Status, dismiss and delete
sections.text:
An action's status is **New**, **In Progress**, **On Hold**, **Completed** or **Dismissed**. The row menu sets In Progress, Completed or Dismiss without opening the action.

Dismissing asks why: it doesn't matter to us, it's already done, the data behind it is wrong, or not now. You can also dismiss without saying why. History shows the reason.

**Delete**, for admins and managers only, removes an action for everyone, and it won't come back on its own the next day.

sections.heading: Inside an action
sections.text:
Click a row to open the action. Under its title you set **Status**, **Assignee** and **Due date**. Its tabs:

- **Overview**: **Why this priority?**, **Why this action?** with the signals behind it, the **Goal** (what done looks like, with a date) and the linked **KPIs**.
- **Affected**: the prompts, pages, topics, competitors or platforms it is about, with each prompt's demand.
- **Tasks**: the work, step by step.
- **Signals**: the evidence. Click one to open it on the Signals tab.
- **History**: every change, from status and assignee changes to tasks updated or sent.

sections.heading: Run an agent on an action
sections.text:
When Chat is on, Admins and Managers see **Run agent** on each open action: an agent button next to its title in the list, and at the top of the open action.

It lists your agents that work on the action's brand, the ones used on this kind of action first. Pick one, and Chat starts a run on this action alone and opens it beside the action. **Run with Chat** does the same without an agent, in your default mode. **Create an agent for this kind of action** starts a new agent from a fitting skill.

The run drafts the work, but closing tasks stays your click. If the action is completed or dismissed, an agent's run stops; a **Run with Chat** run doesn't. The action's **History** shows when a run started and ended, and who started it.

sections.heading: Assign work
sections.text: An action with no one on it belongs to **Everyone** in the workspace until someone takes it. Pick a teammate in the action's **Assignee** field, and set a **Due date** if it has one. The **Assignee** filter on the Actions tab shows one person's actions, or **Everyone** for the unassigned ones.

sections.heading: Export actions
sections.text:
**Export CSV** on the Actions tab downloads the actions in the current view, as filtered, with their priority, status, assignee, due date, task progress and affected items.

Inside an action, **Copy Data** gives the whole action as Markdown to paste into a doc or ticket, and **Export** downloads it as **Export CSV** or **Export Excel**. The Excel file has one sheet each for the action, its affected items, tasks, signals and history.

sections.heading: Send work here from other pages
sections.text:
Most actions come from signals each night, but you can also send work to the Action Center:

- **Mentions**: select answers, or open one, and click **Send to Action Center**.
- **Content**: **Send to Actions** on a content opportunity, or **Assign to…** on a Content Plan row.
- **New content**: send it to a teammate with **Send to Action Center**.
- **Site Audit**: **Send to Action Center** on a page's audit report.
- **AI Referral Traffic**: select pages and click **Send to Action Center**.
- **Brand Visibility**: **Send action** on a topic in Opportunities.
- **Product Visibility**: pick the work in a product's plan and click **Send … actions to Action Center**.
- **Prompts**: **Send Actions** on a prompt's Improve tab.
- **Chat**: **Send to Action Center** under an answer. Its Overview links back to the chat.

Sending the same thing twice doesn't create a second action: the page says it is already in the Action Center.

articles.title: Track KPIs in the Action Center

sections.text: The **KPIs** tab tracks the goals you set for the brand. Each KPI shows its **Value**, **Change**, **Trend (7D)**, **Goal**, progress **vs Goal** and a **Status**. An action's Overview lists the KPIs it is linked to.

sections.heading: KPIs you can track
sections.text:
AI Visibility, Citations, Mentions, Share of Voice, AI Referral Traffic and Positive Sentiment.

A brand that never had KPIs starts with a suggested set: AI Visibility, Citations, Mentions, Share of Voice and Positive Sentiment, plus AI Referral Traffic when Google Analytics is connected. Each aims 20% above its last 30 days, or starts from a default where there's no data yet. It is saved the first time an admin or manager opens the tab.

sections.heading: KPI status
sections.text:
- **Goal Reached**: 100% of the goal or more.
- **On Track**: 70% or more, and not moving the wrong way.
- **At Risk**: 40 to 69%, or moving the wrong way before the goal is reached.
- **Off Track**: under 40%.

sections.heading: Change your KPIs
sections.text: Click **Edit KPIs** (or **Configure KPIs**) to open the framework. Pick a template (**AI Search Visibility**, **Brand Monitoring** or **Custom Framework**; **Content Performance** is marked coming soon), a time period (Weekly, Monthly or Quarterly) and a target for each KPI, then click **Save & Apply**. Only admins and managers can change KPIs.

articles.title: Action Center overview

sections.text: The **Action Center** is where Ansvisor turns what changed in AI search into a ranked list of work. It is the first page you see after you sign in. Everything in it is per brand: switch brands to see another brand's work.

sections.heading: The tabs
sections.text:
- **Actions**: what to do now, ranked by Priority Score.
- **Signals**: what changed across your AI visibility data.
- **KPIs**: the goals you track for the brand.
- **History**: what was done, and what it moved.

Admins and managers also see **Needs review**, where tasks the AI wrote without some of their details wait for a person.

sections.heading: How the work flows
sections.text: Signals are detected after your daily tracking run. Ansvisor groups related signals into one action, so a long list of findings becomes a few pieces of work. At most five new actions are added per brand per day, so the list stays short enough to act on. Each action comes with tasks. When you close an action as **Completed**, History measures what changed afterwards.

sections.heading: While the first tracking runs
sections.text: While a new brand's first tracking runs, one thin line sits under the tabs: **First tracking running**, how many of its checks are done and about how long is left. If another analysis is running, the line says **First tracking queued** until a slot opens. Click **Details** to read what it means and follow the run on Brand Visibility. Actions, signals and KPIs fill in once it finishes, and the line goes away. Meanwhile, a new brand starts with the **Getting started** steps on the Actions tab.

sections.heading: A weekly routine
sections.text: Work from the **Top Actions** card each week. Assign each action, set a due date, and close it as **Completed** when its tasks are done, so History can measure the result.

articles.title: Signals in the Action Center

sections.text: The **Signals** tab lists what changed: a visibility drop, a lost citation, a competitor gaining, a page with no AI traffic, a site issue. Signals are detected after your daily tracking runs, and they are the evidence actions are built from. Many of the same changes also appear in the Daily Pulse email.

sections.heading: Cards and filters
sections.text:
The cards show Total, Important (high impact), New and Resolved signals, and the average signal impact, for the selected range (7, 30 or 90 days) against the range before.

Filter by category (Visibility, Citation, Mention, Traffic, Technical, Competitor), **Impact**, **Status**, **Source** (AI Results, Google Analytics, Google Search Console, Site Audit) and **Platform**, or search.

sections.heading: Signal status
sections.text: A signal is **New**, **Acknowledged**, **Resolved** or **Dismissed**. Set it from the row menu, and use **Reopen** to bring one back. When you resolve or dismiss a signal, the actions it supports get their Priority Score again right away.

sections.heading: Inside a signal
AI traffic signals
sections.text:
The nightly pass also watches AI Referral Traffic and raises these signals:

- **AI visits fell from … to … week over week**: AI visits over the last 7 whole days fell 40% or more from the 7 before, which had at least 30. It feeds **Recover AI traffic**.
- **Broken AI links on …**: in the last 7 days, AI visitors landed on a missing page that AI answers cite, or three or more landed on another missing page. It feeds **Fix broken citation targets**.
- **AI search bots haven't read … that AI answers cite**: needs 30 days of AI-bot data. It feeds **Fix AI crawler accessibility**.
- **… started sending visitors**: an AI platform sent visits for the first time.

articles.title: Action history and results

sections.text: The **History** tab lists actions once they are In Progress, On Hold, Completed or Dismissed, with what they were meant to do and what has been measured since. A result is measured after the action, not proven to be caused by it.

sections.heading: Find an action in History
sections.text:
Filter by range (7d, 30d, 90d, All), **Status**, **Type**, **Priority** and **Source**, and sort by Newest, Oldest or Priority. The cards count total, completed, in-progress, no-improvement and dismissed actions in the window.

Click an action to see **What was the goal?**, **What happened?** (the signals it was built from), its affected items and tasks, and its **Result**.

sections.heading: How a result is measured
sections.text:
Only a completed action is measured. Its metrics are read three times, over the week ending 7, 14 and 30 days after it closed, each against the 7 days before it was raised. Until the final reading on day 30, the result reads *so far*, and the drawer lists each reading.

An action that names its prompts or pages is measured on them, with the brand-wide figures beside. Its prompts' change is also shown net of the brand's prompts it didn't touch, so a change that hit every prompt, such as an engine's update, is told apart from its own. A Site Audit fix is judged by its pages audited again since it closed.

sections.heading: What a result means
sections.text:
- **Improved**, **Mixed**, **No meaningful change** or **Declined**: judged by the action's main metric, the first one it names. **Mixed** means another metric it names moved the other way.
- **Not measured**: the action was dismissed.
- **Not measurable**: it has no metric to read, or its main metric is mentions or citations and tracking missed more than two nights in one of its weeks.

The drawer also says what became of the signals that raised it: how many ended, turned into another, were dismissed, or are still open.

sections.heading: Actions sent from Improve
sections.text: An action sent from a prompt's Improve tab reports on how many platforms its position improved. It is read again daily while the action is open, and for 30 days after it is completed.

sections.heading: The Scorecard
sections.text: Switch History from **Actions** to **Scorecard** to see what each kind of action did at this brand over the range, 90 days unless you pick another. It shows how many were completed, their results so far, the **Success rate** (the share of results that improved, shown once a kind has three), the median change in each action's main metric, and how many were dismissed, with the reason given most often. It counts this brand's own actions only.

sections.heading: When a problem comes back
sections.text: When an action is closed, its condition can open a new action after a two-week rest if it is still firing. The old one stays in History as the record of that round of work.

articles.title: Action Priority Score

sections.text: Every action has a **Priority Score** from 0 to 100: how soon to work on it beside the others. Impact says how much an action could matter; priority weighs impact together with the evidence behind it. The score sets the default order of the **Actions** tab and the **Top Actions** card.

sections.heading: Priority levels
sections.text:
- **Critical**: 90 and above.
- **High**: 75 to 89.
- **Medium**: 50 to 74.
- **Low**: below 50.

sections.heading: What goes into the score
sections.text:
- **Impact**: the action's impact grade, high, medium or low.
- **Demand**: how much its prompts, search queries or pages are searched or visited. Only the most demanded few count. A prompt's measured demand level raises it: High more, Medium a little.
- **Severity**: a loss ranks above a sharp drop, a drop above a slip, and a slip above a gap or a site issue.
- **Business value**: how commercial the searches are, or what a page is worth from Google Analytics.
- **Confidence**: how many independent kinds of finding and data sources agree.
- **Recoverability**: ground you held and lost is nearer at hand than ground you never held.
- **Recency**: newer evidence counts more.

Demand or business value that nothing measures neither raises nor lowers the score.

sections.heading: Past success
sections.text: On top of these, past success nudges the score: how this brand's own earlier actions of the same kind turned out over the last six months, as the History scorecard counts them. A kind that improved results here sits up to 10 points higher, one that rarely did up to 10 lower. A few results barely move it, and a kind with no results yet doesn't move at all. Other brands' results are never used.

sections.heading: When the score changes
sections.text:
An action is scored when it is created, and again every night from that night's evidence. When you resolve or dismiss a signal, the actions it supports are scored again right away. An action not scored yet shows a dash and sorts after the scored ones.

An action sent from another page has no detection signals, so it is scored from what it carries, such as the prompts or pages that were sent.

sections.heading: Why this priority?
sections.text: The action's **Overview** tab starts with **Why this priority?**: one sentence written from the facts the score rests on. It says what changed, on what, how recently, and what makes it matter. When past success moves the score by a point or more, it says so too.

sections.heading: Not the Content Plan's score
sections.text: The Content Plan has its own Priority Score, which ranks the Plan's pages. The two are worked out separately.

articles.title: Action tasks and how they are checked

sections.text: Each action comes with tasks: concrete steps such as "Refresh content for these prompts" or "Add structured data to these pages". You find them on the action's **Tasks** tab.

sections.heading: What a task tells you
How we check
sections.text:
**How we check** says how a task is confirmed:

- **Automatic**: Ansvisor fetches the page again.
- **Re-run**: the prompts run again.
- **Manual**: you confirm it.

Automatic checks run every night, and when you click **Check now**. Only pages on the brand's own site are read. A task that passes is completed by itself, and History says so. One that doesn't shows **Last check** with what is still missing. Site Audit fixes are checked by your next audit.

sections.heading: What an automatic check looks for
sections.text:
- **A broken page**: the page answers again.
- **Publishing**: the page answers where it wasn't before.
- **Structured data**: the audit checks that raised the action now pass on the page.
- **Crawler access**: robots.txt lets the AI crawlers in, and the page isn't noindex.
- **Optimizing or refreshing**: the page changed by more than a date, a price or a rotating quote. Blocks that change by themselves, such as the latest posts, don't count.
- **New text**: the task's new text is on the page, and the text it replaces is gone.

A task you reopen after it passed stays open: the call is yours.

sections.heading: Task status
sections.text: A task's status is **To Do**, **In Progress**, **Completed**, **Skipped** (with a reason), **Waiting Approval**, or **Failed** when Ansvisor couldn't carry it out itself and it needs doing by hand. Skipped tasks leave the count, so they don't hold an action short of done. Use **Add task** for work of your own, and delete tasks you don't need.

sections.heading: Hand a task on
sections.text:
From a task you can:

- **Create content** or **Optimize page**: open a draft in the Content Editor for this task. **Open draft** returns to it, and marking the draft ready completes the task.
- **Send to Content**: send a content task to Content as an opportunity, where a brief can be written for it.
- **Send to webhook**: post the task to the brand's webhook, for a workflow outside Ansvisor. Set it up under **Content › Webhook Settings** with the **Action Center task sent** event selected.

sections.heading: Files attached from Chat
sections.text:
When Chat attaches a file or a draft to a task, the task's details list it under **Attached from Chat**: its name, who attached it, when, and **Open**. A draft opens in the Content Editor; any other file downloads. A paperclip with a count shows on the task row.

Each attachment is also a line in the action's **History**, as is a task Chat set to **Ready for review**. Neither changes the task's status: you mark it done yourself.

sections.heading: Regenerate tasks
sections.text:
Where AI task writing is on for your workspace, **Regenerate tasks** writes the action's tasks again from its evidence, in your brand's terms, by the **Site type** in the brand settings. Done, under-way and hand-added tasks stay. It uses your plan's monthly AI allowance.

The AI also reads this brand's last three closed rounds of the same action. It builds on what improved results here, and doesn't hand out again a task that was done without effect. A task it writes without its URL, Change, Done when or How we check waits on **Needs review**.

sections.heading: Tasks Ansvisor does itself
sections.text: Some tasks that only read data, such as checking a page's traffic in your connected Analytics, can be carried out by Ansvisor overnight. The action's History says so. Nothing that would change something outside Ansvisor runs without your approval: such a task waits as **Waiting Approval**.

sections.heading: Comparing pages overnight
sections.text:
Two tasks compare pages for you overnight:

- **Compare competitor content and coverage** reads up to three pages AI answers cited for the action's prompts, your competitors' first, and your own cited page. It says which checks at least half of their pages pass that yours doesn't.
- **Find what sets your winning pages apart** compares up to three of your winning pages with your other pages that Site Audit checked. It lists what most winning pages have and the others lack, and the pages missing the most of it.

When there is nothing to compare, the task stays open with the reason, and Ansvisor tries again a week later.

articles.title: Getting started steps in the Action Center

sections.text: A new brand starts with **Getting started**: a fixed list of 17 steps on the Action Center's **Actions** tab. While it runs, the **Getting started** category opens first and lists the steps with their **Stage**, **Status** and **Ready** time, and a **Getting started** card shows how many are done. Click **All** or another category to see your actions.

sections.heading: The four stages
sections.text:
- **Set up**, ready now: set your KPIs, add at least 3 competitors and 3 topics, add 3 prompts per topic, connect Google Search Console and Google Analytics, and add the AI Traffic snippet.
- **Explore**, when the first AI answers are in (usually within an hour): see where you stand in Brand Visibility, read your first AI answers, track high-value prompt suggestions, check what AI says about you, see who AI quotes and see visits from AI.
- **Act**, when the first content suggestions are in (about 24 hours): pick content from suggestions, create your first content, optimize a page.
- **Ready**, after every step above is done or skipped.

The high-value prompts step waits about 24 hours after you connect Search Console or Analytics.

sections.heading: Complete a step
sections.text: Click a step to open its card: why it matters, how to do it, and when it counts as done. The card's button opens the step's page in a new tab. Most steps are checked automatically from your data, such as three competitors saved or a first AI visit detected, so the step updates when you come back to the Action Center tab. A step still waiting for its data says when it opens.

sections.heading: While the first tracking runs
sections.text: A new brand's first tracking takes from a few minutes to an hour or two at busy times. Meanwhile, the steps you can do right away come first and carry a **Ready now** mark: KPIs, competitors, topics and prompts you haven't finished, Google Search Console, Google Analytics and the AI Traffic snippet. The steps that need the first answers say **Arriving now**. Their card shows how far tracking is, such as "Your first answers are arriving (18 of 40) · ~6 min", instead of a page that is still empty. When tracking finishes, the app says **Your first results are ready**, the list goes back to its usual order and those steps open.

sections.heading: Skip the Google steps
sections.text: **Connect Google Search Console** and **Connect Google Analytics** are optional. Admins and managers can **Skip** them. A skipped step counts as complete, and you can still connect later from Settings. Without either one, prompt and content suggestions are less accurate.

sections.heading: Start or skip Getting started
sections.text:
Admins and managers see **Get Started** or **Skip Get Started** at the top right of the Actions tab.

- **Skip Get Started** puts the actions list back to normal. Steps you finished stay done, and you can start again any time from the same button.
- **Get Started** appears after a skip, and for an existing brand whose setup looks incomplete: fewer than 3 competitors or topics, no Search Console, or no content in the last 30 days.
- A brand added to an organization that already has one asks first whether to run Getting started for it. Choose **Run Getting started** or **Skip**.

sections.heading: Steps are not actions
sections.text: Getting started steps are not actions: they have no Priority Score and never come from signals. Your actions are listed beside them, under **All** and the other categories.

articles.title: Review tasks waiting in Needs review

sections.text: A task the AI writes without its **URL**, its **Change**, **Done when** or **How we check** doesn't reach the action's task list. It waits on the Action Center's **Needs review** tab instead, with what it misses. Only admins and managers see the tab and review tasks.

sections.heading: Approve a task
sections.text: Click **Edit**, fill the missing fields and click **Approve**. The task is added after the action's other tasks. All four fields, the URL, the change, Done when and How we check, must be filled before it can be approved.

sections.heading: Dismiss a task
sections.text: Click **Dismiss** on a task you don't want. A dismissed task never reaches its action.

sections.heading: Where these tasks come from
sections.text: They come from AI task writing, such as **Regenerate tasks** on an action. Only the tasks that miss one of the four fields wait here; the others go straight to the action's **Tasks** tab. Tasks of an action that is completed, dismissed or deleted aren't listed.

articles.title: See which AI bots read your site

sections.text: The **AI bots reading your site** section of **AI Traffic Analytics** shows which AI bots read your pages, from your own Cloudflare or Vercel. Only verified bots count: the bot's name and its operator's published addresses must both match. Today that's the bots of OpenAI, Anthropic and Perplexity.

sections.heading: What the section shows
sections.text:
- **By bot type**: hits, pages read and last seen for **Training**, **Search index** and **User fetch**, with the bots under each.
- **Pages AI bots read**: hits per page, and when each type last read it.
- **The search-bot alert**: pages AI answers cited in the last 30 days that no AI search bot read in that time. It starts 30 days after the first AI-bot request, and pauses when the bot data doesn't cover the last 30 days or the month's cap was reached.

sections.heading: Connect AI bots
sections.text:
Click **Connect** on the **AI bots** card in the Data sources strip, and choose how your site sends AI-bot requests: **Cloudflare Worker** (recommended), **Cloudflare Logpush** or **Vercel Drain** (Vercel Pro and Enterprise only). Each option says what it costs on your own Cloudflare or Vercel bill before you connect, and none of them changes your site's speed.

Click **Create connection** and follow the numbered steps. Copy the settings right away: the secret in them isn't shown again. If you lose it, revoke the connection and create a new one.

sections.heading: Manage connections
sections.text: **Manage** on the card lists your connections with their last request, lets you **Revoke** one, and shows this month's use. Cloud plans store a monthly number of detailed rows; past it, detailed rows pause until the next month and the totals are still counted. Cloudflare Logpush and Vercel Drain also have a monthly number of log records; past it, they aren't read until the next month. Only requests to your brand's own domains, or their subdomains, are kept.

sections.heading: Dates and sample data
sections.text:
Bot counts are kept by UTC day, so the 24-hour range reads yesterday and today (UTC), and All time reads the last 90 days.

On the Starter plan, the section shows sample data with **Upgrade**. Without a connection, it offers **Connect** or **Preview with sample data**.

articles.title: AI Referral Traffic page

sections.text: **AI Referral Traffic** in the sidebar opens the **AI Traffic Analytics** page. It measures real visits to your site from AI assistants, what those visits are worth, and whether AI is changing your Google traffic. Most analytics tools count these visits as direct or referral traffic; Ansvisor tells each assistant apart.

sections.heading: Date range and changes
sections.text:
Pick a range: 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d, All or Custom. The page opens on the last 24 hours, then on the range you last picked in this browser, and every section follows it.

Each figure is compared with the period of the same length just before. Below 30 visits in either period, the change reads **Low sample** instead of a percentage. A platform or page with no visits before reads **new**. All time has no previous period.

sections.heading: How visits are counted
sections.text:
- **One visit per session**: a reload, or a further link from the same answer, continues the visit. The visits card gives the pageviews beside the visits.
- **Snippet or Google Analytics, never both**: on days the tracking snippet sent any visit, the page counts the snippet's; on other days, Google Analytics'. The visits card says how many days came from Google Analytics.
- **Recent AI Referral Visits**, at the bottom, shows only the snippet's visits, one row per visit. Search it by address and filter by platform.
- **No snippet, no zero**: until the tracking snippet is seen on your site, the page says **Tracking code not detected** and how to add it, rather than showing 0 visits. Chat and the MCP tools say the same.

sections.heading: Summary line and cards
Trend and platforms
sections.text:
- **AI Referral Trend**: **By platform** shows visits per day, or per hour on 24h. **vs Google clicks** sets AI visits beside Google clicks; it needs Search Console and a range of 7 days or longer. On **vs Google clicks**, dashed lines mark the days actions entered the Action Center or prompts were added.
- **Platform Breakdown**: each AI platform's share of visits.
- **Referrals by Platform**: visits and change per platform, with **Engaged** and **Key events** from Google Analytics.
- **Top Landing Pages**: the pages with the most AI visits, and how often tracked answers cite them.

AI Overviews and AI Mode clicks are part of Google organic clicks, and Google doesn't let them be separated.

sections.heading: Where AI visitors convert
sections.text:
With Google Analytics connected, two tables show what AI visits bring:

- **Top converting pages from AI**: landing pages ranked by key events from AI visits, or by revenue when the property reports it, with the best platform.
- **Which answers bring buyers**: the topics of your tracked prompts whose answers cite those converting pages, by AI platform.

A range with fewer than 30 AI visits uses the last 30 days here, and says so.

sections.heading: Which AI assistants count
sections.text: ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, Gemini, Copilot, Grok, DeepSeek, Meta AI, You.com, Phind, Poe and Google Labs. The snippet also counts Bing's Copilot answer links, as **Bing**. A visit counts when it comes from one of their sites, or from a link tagged with their name. Google Analytics' own **AI Assistant** channel also shows assistants that aren't on the list yet. AI visits that arrive with neither count as Direct. Visits from ChatGPT Shopping product cards show as **ChatGPT Shopping**; they're part of ChatGPT's visits.

sections.heading: Export the page
sections.text: **Export** gives the whole page as **Excel (.xlsx)**, one sheet per section, or **CSV (.zip)**, one file per section. Each table also has its own Excel and CSV buttons. A range with more than 100,000 visits is too large to export at once.

sections.heading: Weekly AI Traffic e-mail
sections.text:
Every Monday, an e-mail about the week before goes to each brand's Daily Pulse recipients, if the brand had AI visits that week or the one before. It shows AI visits with the change, the top platform, the summary line, visits by day and platform, and the top changes.

To turn it off for a brand, untick **AI Traffic weekly digest** in **Settings › Notifications**; admins and managers can change it. It isn't sent while the brand's Daily Pulse is **Off**. The e-mail is on Ansvisor Cloud only.

articles.title: AI traffic by page and Google query

sections.text: The **Pages** section of **AI Traffic Analytics** answers which pages get AI visits, which don't, and why. Below it, the Google Search Console tables show whether AI is changing your Google traffic.

sections.heading: The Pages tabs
sections.text:
- **No AI traffic**: pages with traffic in Google Analytics or in your sitemap that got no AI visit, most valuable first. **AI visibility** says why: **Cited**, **Not cited** or **No prompt**.
- **Cited, not clicked**: pages AI answers cited at least 20 times in the range that got no AI visit.
- **Traffic, no prompt**: pages AI assistants sent visitors to that no tracked prompt's answer cited.
- **Broken AI links**: pages AI visitors landed on that don't exist.
- **All pages**: every page with AI visits, citations, traffic or a sitemap entry in the range.

sections.heading: Next steps from a page
sections.text:
Rows carry their next step: **Audit page** for a page AI cites or a prompt targets, **Add prompts** for one no prompt points to.

On **No AI traffic** and **Cited, not clicked**, each row's **…** menu also has **Send to Action Center**, **Add prompts** and **Suggest content**. Under the list, **Audit N cited pages** (or **Audit N pages**) starts Site Audits for the pages shown, and **Send to Action Center** sends them as one action. Only admins and managers can add prompts or suggest content.

sections.heading: Add prompts for a page
sections.text: **Add prompts** suggests questions people ask AI assistants that the page answers, including ones from its Search Console queries, and lets you add your own. The prompts you track from it point to the page, so their answers show whether AI cites it. Each one uses a prompt slot on your plan.

sections.heading: Fix broken AI links
sections.text:
**Broken AI links** shows what the visitor got: **Not found (404)**, **Gone (410)**, **Shows a not-found page (200)** for a site that shows its own not-found page, or **Page title says not found** where the browser reports no status.

Each comes with a suggested **Redirect to**: a **Similar page**, **The page above it** or the **Home page**. Addresses with a query string get no suggestion. With the tab open, the Excel and CSV buttons export the redirect list. Add the tracking snippet to your 404 page too, so these visits are seen.

sections.heading: Is AI taking Google clicks?
sections.text: With Search Console connected, **Is AI taking Google clicks?** lists pages whose impressions rose 15% or more while their click-through rate fell 20% or more, among pages with at least 100 impressions in the period before. An AI Overview may be answering in place of the click. **Positions** shows whether you're cited for a tracked prompt about the page; **Add prompts** appears when none is about it yet.

sections.heading: Untracked Google queries
sections.text: **Untracked Google queries** lists Search Console queries with clicks that no tracked prompt covers, most clicked first. **Track** adds one as a prompt; **Track all** adds the listed ones that your plan's prompt slots allow. Admins and managers can track queries.

articles.title: Track conversions from AI visits

sections.text: Google Analytics' key events say how many AI sessions converted. To see which pages AI visitors went through on the way to a signup, a demo form or an order, turn on conversions for the brand. The snippet then follows visitors who came from an AI assistant for 30 days, and credits each conversion to the assistant that first sent them.

sections.heading: Turn conversions on
sections.text:
In **Brand Settings › Tracking**, under **Conversions from AI visits**, tick **Track conversions from AI visits** and choose **Consent**:

- **Wait for the visitor's consent** (recommended): no journey is followed until your site says the visitor agreed. AI visits themselves are counted as before.
- **Don't wait: our own banner covers it**: only if your cookie banner already asks for analytics storage, or where no consent is needed.

Conversions are off by default, and only admins and managers can change them.

sections.heading: Replace the tag
sections.text:
Under **Use this tag**, copy the tag with the copy button on its code, and use it in place of the one you have, on every page. The tag carries your choices, so after you change **Consent**, copy it again.

To turn conversions off, untick **Track conversions from AI visits** and put the tag without them back.

sections.heading: Tell Ansvisor when a visitor agrees
sections.text:
With **Wait for the visitor's consent**, your cookie banner has to tell the snippet when the visitor agrees, and when they say no or take consent back. Google Consent Mode needs nothing more. A banner set up inside Google Tag Manager needs a tag there for agreeing and one for refusing.

The visitor has to agree on the page the AI assistant sent them to: agreeing on a later page doesn't bring the journey back.

sections.heading: What counts as a conversion
sections.text:
- A form with an email field counts as a signup on its own, once per page load. Contact and newsletter forms count too, unless you give them their own goal. Login forms don't count, and nothing typed in a form is sent.
- Anything else, such as a thank-you page or a purchase, needs a conversion call from your site's own code.
- On Shopify, orders come from a Customer events pixel. Copy it under **Shopify store** in **Brand Settings › Tracking** and add it in Shopify admin as a custom pixel.

sections.heading: Where you see the results
sections.text: The Content Editor shows what came of it: the **Live page** tab for each page, and the **From AI visits** line on the Content **Plan** for the whole site.

sections.heading: What it can't see
sections.text:
- Visitors who refuse cookies, or who agree only after leaving the page the AI assistant sent them to.
- AI visits that arrive without a referrer: they count as Direct.
- Google's AI Overviews and AI Mode.
- Journeys from one subdomain to another.
- Forms inside an embedded widget, forms sent from a script, and posts without a form. These need a conversion call from your site's code.
- Conversions after the browser has cleared the visitor's id, as Safari can after about a week without a visit to your site.

articles.title: Connect AI traffic data sources

sections.text: The **Data sources** strip at the top of **AI Traffic Analytics** shows the four sources the page reads, and each one's state. A section whose source isn't connected stays on the page with a **Needs …** tag and a **Connect …** button for that source. Only admins and managers can connect a source.

sections.heading: What each source adds
sections.text:
- **Tracking snippet**: AI-referred visits, page by page, as they happen.
- **Google Analytics**: AI visits on days the snippet has none, plus engaged visits, key events, revenue and the AI share of all traffic.
- **Google Search Console**: Google clicks, the pages where AI may be taking them, and the Google queries you don't track yet.
- **AI bots**: which AI bots read your pages, from your own Cloudflare or Vercel, on the Growth plan and above.

sections.heading: Add the tracking snippet
sections.text:
Until the snippet is seen on your site, the page opens with **Tracking code not detected on** your domain, the steps to add it and the snippet itself. **Install** in the Data sources strip opens it too; once the snippet is seen, the button reads **Code**. The page fills in your own address and tracking code, so copy it rather than typing it.

Add it to the head of every page you want to track, your 404 page included, so **Broken AI links** can see visitors who land on a missing page.

sections.heading: Check that the snippet works
What the snippet collects
sections.text:
The snippet sends nothing for a visitor who didn't come from an AI assistant. For an AI-referred visit it sends the page address, the referrer, the AI source, the browser, its language and screen size, and the page's status as the browser saw it. Ansvisor adds the country.

The snippet sets no cookies, and without conversions it stores nothing in the visitor's browser. The visitor's IP address is never stored.

sections.heading: Connect Google Analytics and Search Console
sections.text:
Click **Connect** on either card in the Data sources strip and sign in to Google; access is read-only. If the card then reads **Connected · choose a property for this brand**, pick the property under **Manage**, in **Settings › Integrations**. Connections are shared across your organization.

On a self-hosted server, both cards read **Not set up on this server** until the server has its Google connection keys.

sections.heading: When the first numbers arrive
sections.text: Google Analytics' first numbers arrive in about 15 minutes; up to 14 months of history can take up to 24 hours. Search Console's can take up to 48 hours, because Google reports about two days late.

articles.title: Citations page

sections.text: The **Citations** page lists the domains and URLs that AI engines cited in their answers to your tracked prompts, for the brand selected in the sidebar. It shows which sources AI engines rely on when they answer questions in your category, and sorts them by source type. It reads the answers your tracking already collects.

sections.heading: Filters
sections.text:
- **Date Range**: 24h (the default), 7d, 30d, 90d, All or Custom.
- **Topic**: one topic. It's shown only when the brand has topics.
- **Prompt**: one tracked prompt; type to search the list.
- **Platform**: one AI platform, or all of them.
- **Region**: one region the answers were tracked in, or all of them.

The filters are kept in the page's address, so a refresh or a shared link opens the same view. When a table is empty for the window but the brand has citations outside it, **Show all data** clears the filters and shows all dates and all sources.

sections.heading: Summary cards
sections.text:
Three cards sit at the top of the page:

- **Total Citations**: every citation in the window, across the tracked results (AI answers) in it.
- **Unique Domains**: the cited domains in the source choice you made (**Brand**, **Competitors**, **Third-Party** or **All**), with their unique URLs.
- **Avg citations per result**: the number of links per AI answer.

sections.heading: Top Sources and the source choice
sections.text:
The **Top Sources** card has four tabs: **Domains**, **URLs**, **Competitor Gaps** and **Source Types**.

Above the Domains and URLs tables, four buttons choose which sources they list:

- **Brand** (the default): your brand's own domains.
- **Competitors**: the domains of the competitors you track.
- **Third-Party**: every other site.
- **All**: every source.

The choice doesn't change **Total Citations**, **Avg citations per result**, **Competitor Gaps** or **Source Types**.

sections.heading: The Domains tab
sections.text:
The **Domains** tab ranks each cited domain by how often it was cited, with these columns:

- **Domain**: the domain, its source type, and a link that opens the site.
- **Platforms**: the AI platforms whose answers cited it.
- **Usage**: the share of tracked answers in the window that cite it.
- **Avg Citations**: how many times an answer that cites the domain cites it, on average.

On a domain that isn't yours or a tracked competitor's, the **+** button (**Add as competitor**) opens a dialog with a name taken from the domain. Edit the name and click **Add** to track it on the **Competitors** page.

sections.heading: The URLs tab
sections.text:
The **URLs** tab ranks each cited page by its citations, with **Platforms**, **Usage** and **Citations**. Click a page's title to open its own page in Ansvisor, with every answer that cited it; the small icon beside the title opens the page itself.

The tab lists up to the 2,000 most-cited URLs, and its count gives the full number. Both the Domains and URLs tables show 100 rows a page.

sections.heading: Export CSV
sections.text:
**Export CSV** in the page header downloads the open tab, with the filters applied:

- **Domains**: each domain with its source type, citations, the answers citing it, its usage and the AI platforms.
- **URLs**: each page with its domain, source type, title, citations, the answers citing it and its usage.
- **Competitor Gaps**: the gap list, with each domain's source type, competitor answers, competitors and strength.

**Source Types** has no export.

sections.heading: Source types
sections.text:
Ansvisor gives every cited domain one of eight types:

- **You**: your brand's domains and their subdomains.
- **Competitor**: the domains of the competitors you track, and their subdomains.
- **Editorial**: a fixed list of well-known news, tech and magazine sites.
- **Forum**: forums and question-and-answer sites.
- **Social**: social networks, video sites and blogging platforms.
- **Review**: review and rating sites.
- **Institutional**: .edu, .gov and .mil addresses (country versions included), academic addresses such as .ac.uk, Wikipedia, and a list of public and international bodies.
- **Other**: every site that isn't on one of the lists.

You and Competitor come first: a tracked competitor's domain is always Competitor, even when it's also a review site. Only competitors with a domain are matched. The other lists are short, so most sites are Other.

sections.heading: The Source Types tab
sections.text: The **Source Types** tab shows the cited domains in a donut chart, with each type's share of the domains, not of the citations. It covers every cited domain in the window, whatever the source choice above the tables.

sections.heading: How to use the page
sections.text:
- **See which of your pages AI cites**: keep **Brand**, the default, and open the **URLs** tab. It lists your own pages that AI cites, on which platforms and how often. Open a page to see the prompts it's cited for.
- **Find the third-party sources AI trusts**: choose **Third-Party**. The top of the Domains and URLs lists are the sites AI leans on most for your prompts: places to be mentioned or cited.
- **Watch your competitors' pages**: choose **Competitors** to see which competitor domains and pages AI cites in your answers.
- **Find outreach targets**: the **Competitor Gaps** tab lists the third-party sites AI cites when it names a competitor and not you.

articles.title: Details of a cited URL

sections.text: Every URL that AI engines cite has its own page in Ansvisor. Open it from the **URLs** tab of the **Citations** page by clicking a page's title. It opens with the Citations page's date range, platform and region, but not its topic or prompt. You can change the date range and platform on the URL's page. **Citations** at the top goes back.

sections.heading: The header
sections.text:
The header shows the page's title and address, and its source type. When Ansvisor can tell from the address and title, it also shows the article type: **Topic Guide**, **How-to Guide**, **Review**, **Ranked List** or **Comparison**.

Your own pages are marked **Owned**. Any other page has **Add as competitor**, which adds the page's domain to your tracked competitors.

sections.heading: The summary cards
sections.text:
Five cards sum the page up:

- **Total citations**: how many times AI answers cited it in the window.
- **Answers citing**: how many answers cited it.
- **Prompts**: how many prompts those answers came from.
- **Platforms**: how many AI platforms cited it, and which.
- **Last seen**: when it was last cited, with the date it was first seen.

sections.heading: Extra cards for your own pages
sections.text:
On a page of your own, two more cards appear:

- **Targeted in N prompts**: the prompts that list this page in their **Target URLs**, and how many times it was cited for each.
- **AI-referred visits**: visits to this page from AI platforms in the window, by platform.

sections.heading: Cited in
sections.text:
**Cited in** lists every AI answer in the window that cites the page, newest first, 10 a page:

- **Date**: when the answer was tracked.
- **Platform**: the AI platform that gave the answer.
- **Prompt**: the prompt; click it to open the prompt's page.
- **Sentiment**: the answer's sentiment.
- **Brand mentioned**: a check when the AI answer names your brand. It says nothing about the cited page's own text.
- **Position**: where the page's first citation sits among the answer's citations: **Early**, **Mid** or **Late**, with its number, such as #2 of 7.

sections.heading: Prompts breakdown
sections.text: **Prompts breakdown** lists the prompts whose answers cite the page, with **Answers**, **Citations** and **Last seen**, the most citations first. Use it to see exactly which questions lead AI engines to this page.

sections.heading: Use what you find
sections.text:
- On one of your own pages, **Cited in** and **Prompts breakdown** show the prompts AI engines cite it for, on which platforms and how often.
- A third-party page that AI engines lean on for your prompts is a place to be mentioned or cited.
- A competitor's page shows which of your prompts send AI engines to that competitor. **Add as competitor** starts tracking a site that isn't on your list yet.

articles.title: Find where competitors are cited and you aren't

sections.text: **Competitor Gaps** is a tab of the **Top Sources** card on the **Citations** page. It lists the third-party domains that AI engines cite when they name a competitor and not you. These are outreach targets: sites AI engines already trust for your prompts, where a mention or a citation of your own is missing.

sections.heading: Gap list
By competitor
How Strength works
sections.text:
**Strength** weighs each answer by how many sources it had, so a source in a two-source answer counts more than one in a twenty-source answer. Hover **How this works** beside the views for a short note on the method.

When your brand appears in fewer than one answer in ten in the window, a note says the list may be broad. Work on your baseline visibility first.

sections.heading: Filters and export
sections.text:
Competitor Gaps follows the page's date, topic, prompt, platform and region filters. It doesn't follow the **Brand**, **Competitors**, **Third-Party** or **All** choice above the Domains and URLs tables.

**Export CSV** in the page header, with this tab open, downloads the gap list: each domain with its source type, competitor answers, competitors and strength.

sections.heading: Close a gap with these sources
sections.text:
1. On the **Competitors** page, find the prompts where a competitor leads you, under **Gaps**.
2. Here, in **By competitor**, see the sources AI cites with that competitor and not with you.
3. Create content for the prompt in **Content**.
4. Publish it, earn placements on those sources, and watch the prompt in the head-to-head comparison as new answers are tracked.

articles.title: Add competitors to track

sections.text: Competitors are the brands Ansvisor compares with yours in AI answers to your tracked prompts. You add and remove them on the **Competitors** page, right under **Reports** in the sidebar, and each one then appears in **Tracked Competitors** for a head-to-head comparison.

sections.heading: Open the Competitors page
Add a competitor
sections.text:
Click **Add Competitor** and fill in:

- **Name**: as AI answers write it, not the web address. Ansvisor looks for the name in every answer.
- **Domain** (optional): Ansvisor also looks for the domain in answers, counts citations of the competitor's pages, and marks those pages **Competitor** on the **Citations** page. The card that follows the competitor's pages over time needs it too.

Click **Add**.

sections.heading: Suggest competitors
sections.text:
**Suggest competitors** researches your brand on the web, from its website, region and language, and lists competitors with their domains. The ones you already track are left out.

All suggestions come ticked: untick the ones you don't want and click **Add N competitors**. **Refresh suggestions** asks again. The brand needs a website first.

sections.heading: Add a competitor from Citations
sections.text: On the **Citations** page, the **+** button (**Add as competitor**) on a cited domain that isn't yours or a tracked competitor's opens a dialog with a name taken from the domain. Edit the name and click **Add**. A cited URL's own page has **Add as competitor** too, which adds its domain.

sections.heading: When a new competitor is counted
sections.text:
A competitor is counted in the answers tracked after you add it; earlier answers aren't counted again. Until an answer in the date range is measured for it, its card says **No data**.

When a competitor is added, Ansvisor also reads back 90 days of your answers once, to find the first time AI cited one of its pages.

sections.heading: How many to track
sections.text:
The Getting started step asks for at least 3 competitors, and 5 to 20 give the clearest picture.

AI answers to your prompts may name brands you've never heard of. They are the alternatives people see when you're not cited. Add the most-mentioned ones to your competitors to track them properly.

sections.heading: Remove a competitor
sections.text: Hover the competitor's card in **Tracked Competitors**, click the bin icon, then **Yes, remove competitor**. It's no longer tracked. Past results keep their numbers, but they can't be linked back to the competitor.

sections.heading: When the workspace is read-only
sections.text: On Ansvisor Cloud, while the workspace is read-only, **Add Competitor**, **Suggest competitors** and removing a competitor open the plan dialog instead.

articles.title: Compare your AI visibility with competitors

sections.text: The **Competitors** page, right under **Reports** in the sidebar, compares the AI visibility of the competitors you track with yours, across your tracked prompts and AI platforms. You can also open it with **Head-to-Head** on the **Leaderboard** card of **Brand Visibility**, or by clicking a competitor's name there. **Tracked Competitors** lists them with their visibility; select one to see it head-to-head with your brand.

sections.heading: Tracked Competitors
sections.text:
The **Tracked Competitors** card lists every competitor with its domain and:

- its AI Visibility Score from 0 to 100, the same score as on the Brand Visibility leaderboard: how often answers name it, cite its site, and how early it's named. Hover the score to see its answers, citations and position factor.
- the prompts it's visible in, out of the prompts with answers in the window, such as 12/40 prompts.

**No data** means no answer in the window was measured for that competitor yet, for example one you've just added.

The **Date Range** at the top (7d, 30d by default, 90d, All or Custom) sets the window for these scores. **Export CSV** on the card downloads your brand's and every competitor's scores, with their visible prompts, mentions and citations.

sections.heading: Open a head-to-head comparison
sections.text:
Click a competitor's card to compare it with your brand under **Your brand vs competitor**, with both names filled in. Click the card again to close the comparison. The selected competitor is kept in the page's address, so a refresh or a shared link opens the same one.

The comparison reads every tracked answer, not just the date range. Its scores are each answer's own visibility score from 0 to 100, for your brand and for the competitor.

When there's nothing to compare yet, it says **No comparison data**: run tracking for your prompts first.

sections.heading: Scores and Platform Breakdown
sections.text:
At the top of the comparison, **Your Avg. Score**, **Their Avg. Score** and **Score Difference** show your average score, the competitor's, and the difference between them.

**Platform Breakdown** shows your average and the competitor's on each AI platform, with the difference. A competitor can lead on one platform and trail on another, so aim your work at the platforms where it's ahead.

sections.heading: Gaps and Strengths
sections.text:
- **Gaps** lists up to 10 prompt and platform combinations where the competitor scores higher, grouped by prompt, the widest gap first.
- **Strengths** lists up to 10 where you score higher, your biggest lead first.

A prompt with several platforms opens to show each one.

sections.heading: Prompt-by-Prompt Comparison
sections.text:
**Prompt-by-Prompt Comparison** lists every prompt with **You**, **Them** and **Diff**, the most recently run first.

Click a prompt to see each platform, with its model and region, and how many runs it has. Click a platform with more than one run to see its **Previous runs**, with the date, both scores, the difference and the sentiment. The eye icon opens an AI answer.

**Export CSV** beside the comparison's title downloads it per prompt and platform: the model, region, runs, both scores, the difference and the latest run.

sections.heading: The competitor's pages over time
sections.text:
Below the comparison, a card shows why the competitor may be rising. Its chart shows the answers that mentioned the competitor, and your brand, each week for the last twelve weeks. A marker sits on each week something happened to its pages; the events are listed newest first:

- **First cited in your tracked answers**: the first day an AI answer to one of your prompts cited one of its pages. When a competitor is added, Ansvisor reads back 90 days of your answers once, so the first date is the first within that window.
- **Changed**: once a week, Ansvisor reads again the 10 competitor pages your answers cited most over the last two weeks. When a page's words changed by more than a date or a price moving, it says so, with the Site Audit checks it gained or lost, such as an FAQ or a table.

sections.heading: How the pages are read
sections.text:
The card needs the competitor's domain to find its pages. Pages are read for free from their public address, within a few reads a day, never from a site whose robots.txt keeps crawlers out. The brand's daily page reads are shared with the Action Center's tasks, which go first.

Only what Site Audit's checks found and a summary of the page's words are kept, never its text. Nothing is compared with another brand's answers.

sections.heading: Close a visibility gap
sections.text:
1. On **Gaps**, find the prompts where the competitor leads most.
2. Open the AI answer with the eye icon: what is the competitor named or cited for? The pages-over-time card shows whether its pages changed, and **Competitor Gaps** on the **Citations** page lists the sources AI cites with the competitor and not with you.
3. Create content for that prompt in **Content**.
4. Publish it, earn placements on those sources, and watch the prompt in the comparison as new answers are tracked.

articles.title: Connect Webflow, WordPress, Framer or Wix

sections.text: To send Content Editor pages straight to your CMS, connect it in **Settings › Integrations** with the brand selected. Each brand connects its own Webflow site, WordPress site, Framer project or Wix site. Only admins and managers can connect, change or disconnect a CMS; members see where the brand's pages go.

sections.heading: Connect Webflow
sections.text:
In the **Webflow** card, open **How to get a site token** and follow its steps to generate a site token in Webflow. Webflow shows the token only once. Paste it in **Site token** and click **Connect**.

Then pick the **Collection** your pages go to, your blog's for example. If the token reaches more than one site, pick the **Site** first. Under **Which field takes what**, choose the field for the page content and, if you like, the meta title, meta description, structured data and date. The page's title and slug always go to the item's Name and Slug. Click **Save**. If the collection requires a field Ansvisor doesn't fill, **Save** names it: make it optional in Webflow first.

sections.heading: Connect WordPress
sections.text:
In WordPress, sign in as the user pages should be written by. A separate user with the **Author** role is enough, since Ansvisor writes drafts only. Under **Users › Profile**, add an **Application Password** named Ansvisor and copy it; WordPress shows it once.

In the **WordPress** card, enter the **Site address** as you visit the site, the **User** and the **Application Password**, and click **Connect**. Paste the Application Password, not the user's own password. The site must use https. Ansvisor checks the site before it keeps anything.

sections.heading: If WordPress won't connect
sections.text:
A message says why. The most common fixes:

- WordPress refused the user or password: check the user name, and paste the Application Password.
- There's no WordPress at that address: check the address, and in WordPress set **Settings › Permalinks** to anything but **Plain**.
- Application Passwords are turned off: update WordPress, and allow them in your security plugin.
- The site refused the request: a firewall or security plugin is blocking it, so allow it.
- This user can't write posts: use an Author, an Editor or an Administrator.

sections.heading: Connect Framer
sections.text:
In Framer, open the project's **Site Settings › General** and make a key, as a user who can edit the CMS, then copy it. In the **Framer** card, paste the **Project address** as your browser shows it in Framer, and the key, and click **Connect**.

Pick the **Collection** your pages go to, then which field takes the title and the page content and, if you like, the meta title, meta description and structured data. Click **Save**. A collection with a required field Ansvisor can't fill is marked in the list and can't be saved: make that field optional in Framer first.

sections.heading: Connect Wix
sections.text: The site needs the Wix Blog: pages go there as draft posts. In Wix, the site's owner opens **Account Settings › API Keys Manager**, clicks **Generate API Key**, picks the site, gives the key **Manage Blog** and **Manage Ricos Document**, and copies it; Wix shows it once. In the **Wix** card, paste the **Site id** (or the whole address of the site's dashboard) and the **API key**, and click **Connect**. A Blog with no post can't be connected yet: write one post on it as the site's owner first.

sections.heading: Replace or disconnect
sections.text: Each card has its own way to change the sign-in: **Replace token** for Webflow, **Change sign-in** for WordPress, **Replace key** for Framer and **Change API key** for Wix. **Disconnect** removes the connection; pages already sent stay in your CMS. Framer and Wix don't let Ansvisor revoke a key, so delete it there too: in the project's **Site Settings › General**, or in Wix's **API Keys Manager**. If the CMS refuses the saved sign-in, the card says so, for example **Sign-in refused** or **Key refused**, and asks for a new one.

sections.heading: Send through your workflow instead
sections.text: Pages can also go to your workflow tool, such as n8n, Make or Zapier, which creates the post in your CMS and decides whether it lands as a draft or goes live. On the **Opportunities** page, open **Webhook Settings**, enter your workflow's address in **Webhook URL**, tick **Content page sent**, which is off by default, and save. Pages you send to **Your workflow** then reach it.

articles.title: Generate a content brief

sections.text: A content brief tells a writer what to write to close an opportunity's gap: the title, the type of content, the outline and the keywords. Ansvisor writes it with AI from the opportunity's data, in your brand's language. You can then write the page in the Content Editor, or hand the work on to the Action Center or your workflow tool.

sections.heading: Generate a brief
sections.text:
On **Opportunities**, click an opportunity's title. The panel shows its source data and any brief it already has. Admins and managers click **Generate Brief**.

A brief is written once per opportunity: the button then reads **Brief Generated**. Each brief counts toward the month's content briefs, and on plans with monthly limits **This billing period** shows how many are left.

sections.heading: What a brief holds
Write it, or hand it on
sections.text:
- **Send to Editor** opens **New content** with the opportunity picked; the draft starts with the brief's outline and keywords.
- **Send to Actions** puts the work in the Action Center.
- **Send to Workflow** sends it to your workflow tool.

Earned opportunities don't go to the editor: send them to the Action Center or your workflow tool.

sections.heading: A fresh brief in the editor
sections.text: An opportunity's brief is written once and stays as it is. Once the page is in the Content Editor, **Rebuild brief** there writes a new brief from the sources you keep in the draft.

sections.heading: Send it to your workflow
sections.text:
In the opportunity's **…** menu, click **Send to Workflow**. Ansvisor sends the opportunity, the data behind it and its brief, if it has one, and its status becomes **Sent to Workflow**. The button then reads **Send Again**. To send several at once, tick them on the list and click **Send All**.

The webhook needs **Opportunity sent** ticked. An address that redirects isn't followed, so nothing is sent: use the address it redirects to.

sections.heading: Set up your workflow once
sections.text:
Click **Webhook Settings** at the top of the Opportunities page:

- **Webhook URL**: your workflow tool's address, such as an n8n, Make or Zapier flow, or your own endpoint.
- **Secret Key (optional)**: lets your endpoint tell that a call came from Ansvisor.
- **Events to send**: **Opportunity sent**, **Daily Pulse created**, **Action Center task sent** and **Content page sent**. A new webhook has the first three ticked; **Content page sent** stays off until you tick it.
- **Active**: turn it off to pause sending without deleting the webhook.

**Test Webhook** always sends a test event. Click **Save Webhook** to keep it. Only admins and managers can change or test the webhook.

sections.heading: After the work is done
sections.text:
Once the opportunity is in the Action Center, its status follows its action: **In Progress** once work starts, **Done** when it's complete. Your workflow tool can also move it on, for example to In Progress or Done.

Admins and managers can also tick opportunities on the list and click **Done**.

articles.title: Write a page in the Content Editor

sections.text: The Content Editor is where pages are written. It opens from the Library, from the Plan, or when you start a page in New content. **Editor** in the sidebar takes you back to the draft you last opened for this brand in this browser; with none, or if that draft was deleted or archived, it opens New content. The page saves as you write.

sections.heading: The header
sections.text:
The header shows the title, which you can click to rename the page, and whether your changes are saved. Under them come the page type, the method and status, and a **Rules** chip with how many rules the page meets now; click it to open the rules. On a page that optimizes a live one, a chip counts the cited passages kept.

On the right are the month's AI usage and the buttons **History**, **Copy HTML**, **Export**, **Send to CMS** (the paper-plane icon, for admins and managers) and **Mark ready**, and a button to show or hide the side panel.

sections.heading: Status and runs
sections.text: Where your workspace has Chat, a pill next to the title says where the page stands: **Working** while the Content Agent works on it, **Needs you** while its suggestions wait or the page is in review, **Ready**, **Done** once published, or **Draft**. **Runs** at the top lists your own Chat runs and this brand's Content Agent runs, this page's among them; click one to open it. Once the agent's work has started on the server, its card says you can leave the page: it keeps going.

sections.heading: Write and paste
sections.text:
The page starts with its H1, which is also its title. A page has one H1: the toolbar won't add a second one. A paste keeps headings, lists, links and tables, and drops fonts, colors and styles. Press Command or Ctrl + Shift + V to paste plain text.

**Attach a file** inserts Excel, CSV, Word, Markdown, HTML or text, up to 10 MB each; a sheet comes in as a table. **Add HTML** adds an embed, a widget or a form, kept exactly as written; Ansvisor never runs it. **Edit as HTML** shows the page's source; scripts, iframes and inline styles are removed when you switch back.

sections.heading: Facts and your input
sections.text:
The Content Agent looks up the facts a page needs, such as a price, a plan's limits or a statistic, and links each to the page it came from, never a forum or a social post. A fact no trusted page has is left out of its sentence.

A fact it couldn't look up stays in square brackets for you, as do up to three only your brand has, such as your customer count. Each is tinted amber; **Your input needed** in the toolbar counts them and jumps to the next one, selected so you can type over it.

Ones in alt text, structured data or HTML count too. **Send to CMS** waits until none is left. With Quality on, **Export** offers **Fill now** or **Export without them**, which drops those sentences. One in the title or a heading has to be filled.

sections.heading: The side panel
sections.text:
The side panel's tabs are **Instructions**, **Sources** and **Live page**. **Instructions** holds what the Content Agent follows: **Brief** and **Rules**, and **Quality** when it's on, switched at its top. The panel opens on **Instructions**, on **Rules**.

While the panel is closed, its tabs run down the editor's right edge: click one to open the panel there.

Building the brief and running the Content Agent use your workspace's monthly AI usage.

sections.heading: The brief
sections.text:
**Brief** shows the page type, target URL, goal, audience, length, outline and keywords; **Edit brief** changes them. With no brief yet, **Run Agent** writes the goal, audience and outline from your sources; once there is one, the button reads **Rebuild brief**. Either writes the outline from the sources you keep, each H2 answering a search AI ran for your prompts. If you edited the brief, rebuilding asks first: **Rebuild anyway** or **Keep my brief**.

A draft started from an opportunity with a brief starts with that brief's outline and keywords.

sections.heading: What the brief reads from cited pages
sections.text:
Building the brief also reads a few of the pages AI cited. Their typical length shows beside **Length**, and **Cited pages have** lists what Site Audit's checks find on at least half of them, such as an FAQ schema, tables or statistics. The Content Agent then writes the page toward what its text can carry, not its schema, dates or byline, which your site sets.

Once the brief has an outline, **Rewrite from brief**, for a new page, or **Suggest changes from brief**, for an existing one, hands the page to the Content Agent. The page you have now stays in History.

sections.heading: Sources
sections.text:
**Sources** shows what the draft is built from: **Prompts**, **Fan-outs** (the searches AI ran for your prompts), **Cited pages**, which AI quotes today, and **Search Console** queries. Each source shows where the draft uses it.

Uncheck a source to leave it out, or click **Add source** to add a prompt, a page address or a Search Console query. Then click **Rebuild with selection**.

sections.heading: Live page
sections.text:
For a draft that optimizes a live page, **Live page** shows how that page does now: **Citations**, **AI visits**, **Google clicks** and **Prompts cited**, over 7 days to a year, against the period before. It is not a forecast of what the draft will get.

- Prompts that stopped citing the page are marked **Lost**. **Use the lost prompts in this draft** adds them to the sources and rebuilds the brief.
- **Results from AI visits** shows the AI visits that landed on the page and, with Google Analytics connected, their key events, orders and revenue, by AI source.
- **Your other pages for these prompts** lists your other pages cited for the same prompts.
- With conversions from AI visits on, **Conversions from AI journeys** shows what the journeys through the page brought in.

A new page has nothing to measure until it's marked published with its live address.

sections.heading: Passages AI cites are locked
sections.text: When a draft optimizes a live page brought in by its URL, the passages AI answers quoted in the last 30 days are marked in green, and a chip in the header counts them. The Content Agent never changes these passages. If you edit one, the editor asks first: **Keep wording** or **Edit anyway**. Changing a quoted passage may cost the page those citations.

sections.heading: History, Copy HTML and Export
sections.text:
- **History** keeps earlier versions for 90 days: the live page as imported, the page before agent changes, each Mark ready and publish, each Hand off, and the page before a restore. **Restore** makes a new version, so nothing is lost.
- **Copy HTML** copies the whole page as HTML, HTML blocks and schema included, to paste into your CMS.
- **Export** downloads the page as **Word**, **Excel**, **CSV**, **HTML** or **Markdown**. Excel and CSV hold the page as one row, for a CMS's import. Only the HTML file carries the schema.

With Quality on, **Export** opens a dialog instead: the same files, and under **Platforms** a copy of the page to paste into Webflow, WordPress, Shopify or Google Docs.

sections.heading: Add products from your catalog
sections.text: On an online shop's draft, **Products** in the toolbar adds products from your catalog: search by name, pick one to four that are in stock, and click **Insert**. One shows as a card, more as a grid, each with its picture, name and price, linked to its page. A card keeps its price: to show today's, delete the card and add the product again.

sections.heading: Mark ready
sections.text:
**Mark ready** saves the page, sets it to **Ready** and keeps a version in History. If the draft was sent to the Action Center, it also completes its task there. With Quality on, **Mark ready** opens **Before you publish** first.

Ansvisor doesn't publish the page: copy or export it to your site, or send it to your CMS.

Click **Ready** in the header to move the page back to **In review**. A task that Mark ready completed is open again, unless someone changed it in the Action Center since or the action is closed.

sections.heading: Mark published
sections.text:
Once the page is live, tell Ansvisor where with **Mark published**, in the Library's **Status** menu or, with Quality on, under the header's **Next step** once the page is ready. It asks for the live address, starting from the page it optimizes or your site with the page's slug, and **Live page** measures that address from then. If the draft came from the Action Center, its Publish task is completed once all the action's work is live.

On a published page, the header's **Published** button changes the address. A page your CMS reports live, or one published in Webflow, WordPress, Framer or Wix, gets its address on its own. Restore an archived page in the Library first.

articles.title: Manage drafts in the Content Library

sections.text: The **Library**, under **Content** in the sidebar, lists every page you, your teammates and the Content Agent wrote or changed in Ansvisor. Click a row to open the draft in the editor.

sections.heading: The tabs
sections.text:
Each tab shows its count:

- **All**: every draft that isn't archived.
- **In progress**: drafts being written.
- **In review**: drafts the Content Agent wrote, waiting for a person.
- **Ready**: drafts marked ready.
- **Published**: drafts marked published, by you or your CMS.
- **Archived**: drafts sent to the archive. They keep their status for when they're restored.

sections.heading: Columns and filters
sections.text: The columns are Content, Type, Method (Create or Optimize), By (you, the Content Agent or a teammate), Status, Created and Updated. While the Content Agent writes a draft, its Status reads **Agent writing…**, and **Agent failed** if it couldn't finish; where your workspace has Chat, each comes with the same dot Chat shows for a run. The **Created** filter narrows the list to the last 7, 30 or 90 days. Once a page has been sent to your CMS, the **Last send** filter lists the pages by how their last send went: never sent, sending, sent, failed or published.

sections.heading: The row menu
sections.text:
- **Status**: set the draft to In progress, In review, Ready or Published. Ready works like the editor's Mark ready, and Published, not offered for archived drafts, asks for the page's live address. Moving a ready or published draft back to In progress or In review opens its task again. A published one also opens the action's Publish task again and stops its Live page being measured for the action.
- **Export Word**, **Export Excel**, **Export CSV**, **Export HTML** or **Export Markdown** for that draft.
- **Send to CMS**: send the draft to your CMS, except an archived one. Admins and managers can tick several rows to send up to 25 at once.
- **Send to Archive** or **Restore**.
- **Delete**: the draft leaves the Library for good, with its versions and suggestions. An Action Center task it was sent as stays.

Send to CMS, archiving and deleting are for admins and managers.

sections.heading: Export the list
sections.text:
**Export** in the header downloads the drafts listed, that is the current tab within the **Created** range and the **Last send** filter:

- **Export CSV** and **Export Excel**: one row per draft, with its title, status, method, page type, author, dates, page address, length and text.
- **Export Word**: one document, each draft starting on a page of its own.

sections.heading: Shopping path check for online shops
sections.text:
For an online shop, the **Shopping path** column shows what the last check found for each draft with a shopping path. After each catalog sync, every such draft is read again. A draft needs attention when it links a product that is sold out, refused by Merchant Center or gone from your catalog; hover the mark to see the products. The **Shopping path** filter lists the drafts that need attention, are fine, or have none.

When a published page links a product that no longer sells, a **Fix** action opens in the Action Center, and **Swap in the editor** opens the draft.

articles.title: Find content opportunities

sections.text: The **Opportunities** page, under **Content** in the sidebar, lists content opportunities: what to write or change so AI answers name you where they don't yet. Ansvisor suggests them on its own as tracking data comes in. An opportunity is built for a group of related prompts that one piece of content can answer, or for a single prompt. From each one you can start writing, plan it, brief it or send it on.

sections.heading: What each row shows
Filter, sort and export
sections.text:
- Search the opportunities, and narrow the list by topic, prompt, type, impact, **Source** and status. The sources are **System**, suggested automatically; **Manual**, made with **New**; **Prompt**, suggested from a prompt; and **Action**, sent from an Action Center task.
- **Suggested** picks a period, all time, this month, the last 30 days or your own dates, and the order: highest score, newest or oldest.
- Archived opportunities stay hidden unless you filter to them.
- Most filters and the order stay in the page's address, so a link opens the same view; the topic and the search don't.
