- **Export CSV** downloads every opportunity that matches the filters and the search, not only the page you see.

sections.heading: Quick actions on a row
Work on many at once
sections.text:
Tick rows, or the box in the header for every row shown, then:

- **Send All** sends each one to your workflow tool, which suits kicking off a content sprint.
- **Done**, **Dismiss All** and **Delete** change them all at once. They're for admins and managers.

**Delete** removes the opportunities for good, with any brief they have, and doesn't give back the month's opportunities or briefs. Dismissing keeps them out of your way instead.

sections.heading: Ask for new opportunities
sections.text:
Admins and managers click **New** to get suggestions now, instead of waiting for the next automatic run. Pick a **Focus**: **Let Ansvisor choose**, a **Topic** or a **Prompt**. You can add your own idea, up to 500 characters, and set **How many**.

Opportunities are written per group of prompts: prompts of one topic that a single page could answer, and that already have tracked answers. Each group gets one opportunity; only **Another angle** adds a second take on it.

Titles leave years out unless the need is about one. A year that has passed in an opportunity's title or question shows as this year; your tracked prompts keep their own words.

sections.heading: What each focus picks
sections.text:
- **Let Ansvisor choose** takes the highest-scoring groups that have no opportunity yet, one from each topic first.
- **Topic** takes only that topic's groups.
- **Prompt** takes only that prompt's group, so it writes at most one opportunity, and **How many** stays at 1. If that prompt already has an open opportunity, a message says so when the run ends, with **Open existing**.

sections.heading: No duplicates
sections.text:
Ansvisor never writes the same work twice. When a new opportunity would cover the same need as one you have, because their prompts and AI searches largely overlap, it's added to that one instead and skipped. If nothing new is written, the message says so and counts any duplicates it skipped.

For a second take on the same need, use **Another angle** on the opportunity.

sections.heading: How many you get
sections.text: New opportunities come from a monthly allowance set by your plan, with a cap on how many one request asks for; on limited plans the page shows what's left. Skipped duplicates and opportunities that couldn't be written don't count; **Another angle** counts as one new opportunity. The up to three new opportunities Ansvisor writes by itself each night come from the same allowance.

sections.heading: Owned and earned
sections.text:
Each opportunity has a **Type**. **Owned** means content on your own site. **Earned** means coverage on other sites, such as articles, reviews and links. Some gaps are best closed with a guest post or a press placement rather than a new page of your own.

Earned opportunities don't go to the Content Editor: send them to the Action Center or your workflow tool.

sections.heading: Pick what to work on
sections.text: Don't ship every brief. Editorial time is usually the bottleneck, so pick the two to four high-impact opportunities a week your team can really write, and leave the rest for later.

articles.title: Use the Content plan

sections.text: The **Content plan**, **Plan** under **Content** in the sidebar, ranks what to create, optimize or protect next. It covers the last 7, 30 or 90 days: pick the period at the top right.

sections.heading: The four cards
sections.text:
- **Create**: new pages AI needs, that is open opportunities with no page on your site yet.
- **Optimize**: pages losing ground, and opportunities to improve a page you already have.
- **Protect**: your top pages, cited at least five times in the period and not losing ground, up to five, and opportunities to defend a page.
- **Priority**: rows your team marked as a priority.

Click a card to filter the list to it, and click it again to clear the filter.

sections.heading: When a page is losing ground
sections.text: A page is losing ground when it is cited at least 20% less per tracked answer than in the period before, from at least three citations. Because the comparison is per tracked answer, a week with fewer runs, or prompts added or removed, doesn't move a page. If tracking began during the earlier period, a note above the list says so.

sections.heading: The priority list
sections.text:
Each row shows the **Priority Score**; the **Page**, with its title, page type and path, or **New page**; the **Action**: Create, Optimize or Protect; **Why** it's listed, tagged with where that comes from (**Opportunity**, **Citations** or **Protect**); and **Who** is on it: you, the Agent, a teammate or the person it's assigned to.

The row's button, **Create**, **Optimize** or **View**, opens New content on that row, and **Open draft** opens the draft already being written. Rows marked as a priority come first, the rest by score. The list shows up to 50 rows.

sections.heading: How the Priority Score works
sections.text:
The score runs from 0 to 100 and is built from four factors:

- **Severity**: how urgent the row is. A page losing citations counts most, then a new page AI needs, a page to improve and a page to protect.
- **Opportunity**: the score of the content opportunity behind the row.
- **Page value**: the page's AI visits and, with conversions on, the conversions from AI journeys through it.
- **Citations**: how often AI answers cited the page.

A row without an opportunity, a new page, or a brand with no AI traffic data counts as neutral, not zero. Hover the score to see **How this score is worked out**. Only a page losing citations can reach critical.

sections.heading: The row menu
sections.text:
- **Assign to…**: for a row with a draft, pick a teammate and the draft goes to the Action Center as their task. For a row without one, New content opens with **Team** chosen.
- **Mark as priority** or **Remove priority**: the row moves to the top of the list, tagged **Priority**. **Send to Plan** on an opportunity does the same.
- **Hide from the plan**: the row leaves the list and the counts. Undo it from the message that appears, or later from the hidden rows under the list, with **Show again**.

Only admins and managers can mark priorities and hide rows.

sections.heading: What AI cites in your topics
sections.text:
A line above the list shows what visitors from AI assistants did on your site in the period: visits and, with Google Analytics connected, key events, orders and revenue.

Under **What AI cites in your topics**, click **Show**. For each page type, it compares the share of AI citations that go to that type with its share of your own cited pages. A type AI cites 10 points or more beyond your own mix is marked as a **Gap**. Click a row to filter the priority list to that page type; click it again, or **Clear**, to remove the filter. The page types follow your brand's **Site type** in the brand settings.

sections.heading: Shopping opportunities
sections.text:
For an online shop whose product catalog, in **Settings › Integrations**, has categories, **Shopping opportunities** above the list shows two kinds of rows:

- **Buying guide · New**: a category with at least three products in stock that no page of yours guides shoppers to yet. **Create** starts a buying guide draft and opens it in the editor.
- **Existing post · Fix**: a published post that links a product that no longer sells, or misses some of its category pages. **Optimize** opens it in the editor.

articles.title: Write to the Content Editor rules
synonyms: let the agent fix the page

sections.text: Every page in the Content Editor is written to a set of rules for its page type. The **Rules** chip in the header shows how many the page meets now; click it to open the rules. **Run Agent** asks the Content Agent to suggest changes for the rules the page doesn't meet yet, or to rewrite the whole page to them.

sections.heading: The Rules tab
sections.text: In the side panel, **Instructions** opens on **Rules**. The rules come in five groups: page type rules, length and structure, fan-outs and keywords, links and sources, and style. Most rules can be turned on or off, and many have a value you can change. Each rule's status is read from the page as you write. Rules marked **AI check** are judged by the Content Agent and aren't counted yet.

sections.heading: Save or reset your rules
sections.text: Changes to the rules apply to this draft only. **Save as my rules**, for admins and managers, keeps them for your workspace's next drafts of this page type, and **Reset** goes back to the default set. Under **Your text rules**, write a rule in your own words, or use **Paste many** to add several from a style guide.

sections.heading: Fix open rules with Run Agent
sections.text:
**Run Agent** sits at the top of **Rules**. It asks the Content Agent to suggest small, reviewable changes for the rules the page doesn't meet yet (**Fix open rules**). Its suggestions appear in the page, each with **Accept** and **Reject**, under a bar with **Accept all** and **Reject all**.

A decided suggestion can be taken back with **Undo** or **Restore**, and **Undo all** brings every one back to review. One run makes at most eight changes: run it again for the rules still open. Running the agent uses your workspace's monthly AI usage.

sections.heading: Rewrite the whole page
sections.text:
The **▾** menu beside **Run Agent** also offers **Rewrite the whole page**: one new version written to every rule in the set, with the cited passages kept. It uses more AI usage than fixing open rules. The menu marks it **Recommended** when the page is far off its Length or many rules are open. Pick it, and the button reads **Rewrite page**.

A rewrite comes back as one change: **Compare** it with your page, then **Accept** or **Reject**. Your page before it stays in History. A rewrite isn't offered once the page is ready or published.

When the quoted passages it keeps stop the page reaching its Length, a note offers **Raise Length to …** and **Rewrite, cited passages too**, which may stop those passages being quoted.

sections.heading: Before you run it again
sections.text:
- Accept or reject the open suggestions before you run the agent again or edit the page as HTML.
- The agent doesn't change heading levels: turn extra H1s into H2s in the toolbar yourself.
- The agent only changes drafts, not published pages.

sections.heading: How your choices teach the agent
sections.text: What you accept and reject teaches the agent. For a rule whose suggestions this brand has mostly rejected over the last 90 days (at least five decided, on two pages or more, seven in ten rejected), it keeps its changes as small as the rule allows, and its card says which rules while it works. Only its small changes count: a rejected **Rewrite the whole page** doesn't. Quality's **Hand off** isn't affected.

sections.heading: On a page that is already live
sections.text: When the draft optimizes a live page, the agent is also told how that page does now, as the **Live page** tab shows it over 30 days: how often AI answers cite it and the prompts it lost. It keeps the answers and facts AI engines cite, answers a lost prompt's question where a rule's change can, and its card says what it kept in mind.

articles.title: Open an opportunity and act on it

sections.text: On **Opportunities**, click an opportunity's title to open it in a panel beside the list. The page's address keeps it, so a link opens it too. **Open in new tab**, in the row's **…** menu, opens it as a page of its own. The panel shows what the opportunity rests on, and every action you can take on it.

sections.heading: What it rests on
sections.text:
**Source Data** shows the related prompt, **Est. AI Volume**, your **Current Visibility**, the **Competitor Gap**, the **Strongest Competitor**, the **Search Intent**, the keywords, the searches AI engines ran for the prompt, and the competitors cited.

An opportunity sent from an Action Center task shows that task instead: where, why, how, and when it's done.

**Results** lists the Action Center actions sent from the opportunity, with what changed once their work is complete and measured.

sections.heading: For a group of prompts
sections.text:
An opportunity built for a group of prompts also shows:

- **Your Site**: which of your pages to work on, with their AI citations and sessions over 30 days.
- **Recommended Assets**: the main piece of work and any supporting ones. Each can go to the Action Center on its own.
- **Opportunity Basket**: its prompts, and the searches AI engines ran for them.
- **Why This Score**: demand counts 40%, the visibility gap 30%, the competitor gap 20% and intent 10%, measured over the last 30 days.

sections.heading: The panel's buttons
sections.text:
- **Send to Actions** makes the opportunity an action in the Action Center. The button then reads **Open in Actions**.
- **Generate Brief** writes a content brief. It's for admins and managers, and once the brief is written the button reads **Brief Generated**.
- **Send to Editor** opens **New content** with the opportunity picked: a new page, or the page of yours it names to optimize. Once a draft is being written for it, the button reads **Open draft**. It's offered for owned opportunities that are still open.
- **Export** downloads the opportunity as CSV, Excel or Word.

sections.heading: The … menu
sections.text:
The panel's **…** menu holds the rest:

- **Send to Plan**, for admins and managers: the opportunity goes to the top of the Content plan. Once it's a priority there, it reads **Open in Plan**.
- **Another angle**, except on an opportunity sent from the Action Center.
- **Send to Workflow**, which reads **Send Again** once it's sent.
- **Copy All Data**.
- **Mark as reviewed**, for a new opportunity: its status becomes Reviewed.
- **Restore**, for an archived one: it comes back as New.
- **Dismiss**.

sections.heading: Another angle
sections.text:
**Another angle**, for admins and managers, writes one more opportunity for the same need, with a different content type, format, audience or approach. You can add a direction of your own. Both opportunities stay in the list, so you keep the one you prefer.

It counts as one of the month's new opportunities.

sections.heading: Dismiss an opportunity
sections.text:
**Dismiss**, for admins and managers, asks why:

- **The topic doesn't matter to us** keeps it from being suggested again in this form for 90 days.
- **Right topic, wrong angle** dismisses it and opens **Another angle**, so you can ask for a better take on the same need.

sections.heading: Follow it to Done
sections.text:
Once an opportunity is in the Action Center, its status follows its action: **In Progress** once work on it starts, **Done** when it's complete. Its **Results** card shows what changed once the work has been measured.

A done opportunity comes back as **New**, marked **New signal detected**, when its score has risen since, or the visibility its work gained didn't hold.

articles.title: Check a page's Quality in the Content Editor

sections.text: Quality scores a Content Editor page and lists what would raise it. It's turned on per installation: where it's off, nothing on this page shows. With it on, **Instructions** in the side panel has a third segment, **Quality**, and the header a **Quality** chip with the page's score.

sections.heading: The scores
sections.text:
Quality scores the page from 0 to 100 on **E-E-A-T**, **Trust** and **Readability**: 80 and up is **Strong**, 60 to 79 **Can improve**, and under 60 **Needs work**. The scores are Ansvisor's estimates from Google's published quality signals, not a Google score.

At the bottom, **Site trust**, out of 5, comes from Site Audit's checks of your site, with **Fix in Site Audit** when some are missing.

sections.heading: Your to-dos and what would raise it
sections.text:
- **Your to-dos** are what only you can do, such as picking the page's author, adding your own experience, data or an expert's quote, linking the proof for a claim, and filling the placeholders.
- **What would raise it** lists the checks still open, each with the points it would add to a score and, where it has one, a button such as **Show** or **Add source**.

sections.heading: Hand off
sections.text:
**Hand off** asks the Content Agent to fix the open suggestions in one run, as changes for you to review. Your to-dos stay yours. Each Hand off is kept in the page's History, and it uses your workspace's monthly AI usage.

In **Settings › Content**, admins and managers can have each brand's new pages handed off on their own when they're first opened in the editor.

sections.heading: Next step
sections.text:
With Quality on, the header shows the page's **Next step**: plan the page, write the first draft or bring in your page, fix its length or open rules, add proof and author, or check and mark ready. It comes with a button to take the step, **Skip this step** and **All steps**.

Once the page is ready, **Next step** also offers **Mark published**.

sections.heading: The page's author
sections.text: The header shows the page's author, picked from **Settings › Authors**, or your brand's team as the byline. The Content Agent can't add, edit or invent authors. For a page that advises on health, money or the law, the header also shows the qualified person who reviewed it.

sections.heading: Before you publish
Export with Quality on
sections.text:
**Export** opens a dialog: the same files as without Quality, and under **Platforms** a copy of the page to paste into Webflow, WordPress, Shopify or Google Docs. A line over the options sums up **Before you publish**, and **Review** opens it.

If placeholders are still open, Export asks first: **Fill now**, or **Export without them**, which leaves out the sentences with a placeholder. One in the title or a heading has to be filled.

articles.title: Send a page to your CMS

sections.text: **Send to CMS** sends a Content Editor page to your CMS: into a Webflow or Framer collection as a draft item, to your WordPress site or your Wix site's Blog as a draft post, or to your workflow tool, which creates the post in your CMS. Ansvisor never publishes on its own: you publish in your CMS. Only admins and managers can send pages.

sections.heading: Send one page
sections.text:
In the editor, click the paper-plane icon in the header. With Quality on, **Before you publish** opens first when it has something to ask about, such as a missing author, open placeholders, missing alt text or broken links. Check it and click **Continue to send**. From the Library, open a row's **…** menu and pick **Send to CMS**.

The dialog fills the **Slug**, **Meta title** and **Meta description** from the page; change them before sending if you like. For a regulated page, a selected qualified reviewer is sent separately from its author; the dialog shows both metadata lines. What you send is kept on the draft, so the next send starts from it.

sections.heading: Choose where it goes
sections.text:
The dialog offers each CMS that is connected and ready, Webflow, WordPress, Framer, then Wix, beside **Your workflow**. Your choice is remembered for the brand in your browser.

A CMS that is connected but not ready shows what to fix and can't be picked, for example when its sign-in is refused or no collection is picked. If the dialog can't check a CMS you chose just then, the page goes to your workflow, and the dialog says so with **Try again**.

sections.heading: What holds a send
Send several pages
sections.text: In the Library, tick the rows to send, up to 25 at once, and click **Send to CMS** in the bar above the table. The dialog lists each page as **Ready**, or says why it can't go; a page that can't go is left out, so fix it in the editor. The pages go one after another in the background. You can close the dialog at any time: the Library keeps following them.

sections.heading: See how a send went
sections.text:
Beside each row's status, the Library shows the last send: a clock while it's on its way, a paper plane once it's sent, a red warning when it failed (hover it to see why), and a blue link once it's published (click it to open the live page).

The **Last send** filter beside **Created** lists the pages that were **Never sent**, **Sending**, **Sent**, **Failed** or **Published**. A send to your workflow isn't retried on its own: send a failed page again from the Library.

sections.heading: When a page becomes Published
sections.text: Once you publish the item in Webflow or Framer, or the post in WordPress or Wix, the page becomes **Published** and its address shows in the Library. Ansvisor checks when you open the Library and once a day, for sends from the last 60 days. A page sent to your workflow becomes Published when the workflow reports where it went live. A page whose item or post you deleted reads as removed: send it again to make a new one.

sections.heading: Sending a page again
sections.text: Sending a page again updates the same Webflow or Framer item, the same WordPress draft post, or the same Wix post (a published one gets a new draft version in Wix). Changes to a published Webflow or Framer item go live with your next publish there. WordPress has no draft of a published post, so a page whose post is published, scheduled or private goes as a new draft post: move the text over in WordPress.

sections.heading: What each CMS leaves out
sections.text:
- **Webflow**: Tables become lists; images aren't sent. Reviewer metadata requires a mapped optional Plain Text field; show it in the collection template. Empty meta descriptions use the page's opening words.
- **WordPress**: Reviewer metadata and structured data aren't sent; the adapter can't map custom metadata or repurpose the post author. Set the meta title and structured data in your SEO plugin. Images keep their addresses; no featured image or category is set.
- **Framer**: Tables stay tables; images aren't sent. Reviewer metadata requires a mapped optional string field; show it in the page template. Duplicate slugs stop the send.
- **Wix**: Images, cover images and categories aren't sent. Reviewer metadata is an SEO tag, not visible text; show it in the page template. Resending replaces post text, so add images after the last send.

Add images in your CMS. The slug may change slightly there: lowercase, without accents, with dots turned into dashes.

articles.title: Start a page in New content

sections.text: **New content** starts a page, either a new one or one you already have, written by you, the Content Agent or a teammate. It opens from the Plan and the Library, from a Plan row's button, from **Send to Editor** on an opportunity, and from **Create content** in a prompt's menu on Tracked Prompts. **Editor** in the sidebar opens it too when you have no draft to go back to, or when that draft was deleted or archived.

sections.heading: Create a new page
Optimize a page you have
sections.text:
Pick **Optimize content** to work on an existing page:

- **Page URL**: a page on your brand's site. **Import** brings in its main text, headings, links and schema; menus and footers stay out.
- **Paste text** from Word, Google Docs or a web page. Headings, lists, links and tables are kept.
- **Upload file**: Word, Markdown, HTML or text, up to 10 MB.

sections.heading: Pick the page type
sections.text:
Click **Continue**. Ansvisor picks a **Page type** from the title, the content, the page or the opportunity, and says which. Pick another if it's wrong; you can also change it later in the editor.

The page types on offer follow the brand's **Site type** in the brand settings: B2B SaaS, E-commerce, B2C or Mobile app. A mobile app, for example, gets **Feature page**, **Pricing** and **Help & FAQ** among its types, and no product or destination pages.

For a new page, **Overview** lists your pages AI already cites for the same prompts, with how many of those prompts each one answers, its AI citations and its Google position. Pick **Optimize … instead** on one of those pages to work on it, or **Create a new page**.

sections.heading: Choose who does it
sections.text:
- **Me**, the default: **Open editor** opens the draft for you to write.
- **Agent**: **Start the agent**, and the Content Agent writes a new page, or suggests changes to an existing one, in the background. The editor shows it at work. You can leave: the draft waits in the Library under **In review**. It uses this month's AI usage.
- **Team**: **Send to Action Center** saves the draft in the Library and sends it to the Action Center as an action. Pick a teammate in **Assign to**, or leave it unassigned.

sections.heading: If the agent can't start
sections.text: If this month's AI usage is spent, there's no active subscription, or the agent is already writing another of your team's drafts, the agent doesn't start. The draft stays in the Library for you to write yourself.

articles.title: Add your first brand

sections.text: When you start with Ansvisor, a setup wizard walks you through your first brand. It usually takes a few minutes, and you need the website of the brand you want to track. The wizard has five steps on a self-hosted install and seven on the cloud: the extra two ask what you work on and pick your plan. From the second step on, your progress is saved as you go, so if you leave, you pick up where you stopped.

sections.heading: Step 1: Brand basics
sections.text:
**Set up your brand** asks for three fields:

- **Brand name**: exactly how the brand is named in the wild, not an abbreviation. Mention detection ignores upper and lower case.
- **Website**: your main domain, such as example.com; the https part is already filled in. It's used to recognize citations of your site and to suggest competitors.
- **Describe your brand** (optional, but recommended): one to three sentences on your industry and your audience. It helps Ansvisor suggest better topics, prompts and competitors.

There's no separate industry field: put your industry in the description.

sections.heading: Step 2: Region and language
Step 3: Topics
sections.text:
On **Choose topics to monitor**, Ansvisor uses your brand details and an AI model to suggest topics: themes your customers care about. The first seven come checked.

Check the topics that fit your brand and uncheck any that don't apply, up to 10. You can also type a topic name of your own and add it with **+**. If suggestions can't be fetched, add your own. **Looks good** moves on.

Aim for four to seven topics. Too few gives a narrow view; too many is noisy and hard to read.

sections.heading: Step 4: Prompts
Step 5: Competitors
sections.text:
On **Add your competitors**, Ansvisor suggests competitors for your brand. Check the real rivals, and uncheck or remove the ones that aren't comparable. Add your own with a company name and domain, using the name as it appears in AI answers rather than the website address.

Select at least one competitor to continue. **Start tracking with N competitors** finishes the brand. Competitor tracking is on every plan.

If your site looks like an online store, Ansvisor turns on Product Visibility for the brand and says so on this step. You can turn it off in the brand settings.

sections.heading: Step 6 on the cloud: What do you work on?
sections.text:
Pick what you work on or lead, such as Founders & leaders, Brand & PR, Content or Growth, and your left menu keeps only the sections you need. **Skip: show me everything** keeps every section. You can change it later in **Settings › Account**.

A self-hosted install asks the same the first time you open the dashboard.

sections.heading: Step 7 on the cloud: Plan and checkout
sections.text:
The final step picks your plan, **Starter** or **Growth**, and starts checkout.

While a free trial is on offer, **Choose how to start** lets you pick the trial, **Monthly** or **Yearly**. With the trial you enter card details, nothing is charged until the trial ends, and the step tells you the day of the first charge. The trial comes with an organization's first subscription only. **Buy now**, or a plan without a trial, starts the plan the same day.

Not ready to add a card? **Explore the demo** opens a demo brand with sample data. Your brand stays saved, and its tracking starts when you pick a plan.

A self-hosted install skips this step.

sections.heading: Add another brand later
sections.text: To add another brand, admins and managers pick **Add Brand** in the brand switcher. It walks through the same first five steps. Your plan sets how many brands you can have.

articles.title: Your first results after brand setup

sections.text: When you finish setting up a brand, the first round of questions to the AI engines starts on its own and the dashboard opens. On a self-hosted install it starts right away. On the cloud it starts after the plan and checkout step, whether you start a free trial there or buy the plan. If you explore the demo brand instead, your brand's first run starts when you pick a plan.

sections.heading: How long the first run takes
sections.text:
The first run can take anywhere from a few minutes to one or two hours at busy times. **Brand Visibility** shows that the first tracking is in progress, and fills in with your results as they come back.

You can leave the page: the run keeps going in the background. When your workspace's first results are ready, everyone in it gets one e-mail, **Your first results are ready**, where e-mail is set up, as on the cloud. It's sent once, not for every brand you add.

sections.heading: Where results appear first
sections.text:
While you wait:

- **Brand Visibility** fills in with your first results.
- **Citations** fills in with the addresses of the pages AI answers cite.
- **Prompt Suggestions**, on the **Prompts** page, offers prompt ideas to add to tracking.

sections.heading: Add another brand
sections.text: To add another brand, admins and managers pick **Add Brand** in the brand switcher. It walks through the same first five steps as your first brand: brand basics, region and language, topics, prompts and competitors. Its first run starts when you finish. Your plan sets how many brands you can have.

sections.heading: Add the tracking snippet
sections.text:
Setup doesn't include the tracking snippet. It's an optional step you do separately for **AI Referral Traffic**: real visits that arrive on your site from AI answer engines.

1. Pick **AI Referral Traffic** in the sidebar. Until the snippet sends its first visit, the code is shown at the top of the page. After that, **Code** beside **Tracking snippet** in the **Data sources** strip shows it again.
2. Copy the snippet.
3. Paste it into the head section of your site's pages, just before the head closes. On WordPress, use a header injection plugin; on a static site, edit your template.

Once the snippet sends a visit, **Tracking snippet** in the **Data sources** strip shows it as active, with the time of the last visit.

sections.heading: While the first tracking runs
sections.text: Brand Visibility says **First tracking in progress** at the top until its first results are in. Above the **Tracked Prompts** table, a note says "Your first answers are arriving", with how many are in and about how long is left, and rows still without results say **Arriving now**. Everything fills in when tracking finishes. Meanwhile, do the **Ready now** steps of **Getting started** on the Action Center. When tracking finishes, the app says **Your first results are ready**.

sections.heading: My visibility score is 0
sections.text: Probably nothing is broken. New, niche or B2B brands often start at 0 on most prompts. AI engines need either plenty of training data that mentions your brand, or live citations from trusted sources. The score stays at 0 only while both are missing, and that is exactly what working on your AI visibility changes.

sections.heading: Prompts that include my brand name
sections.text: Remove them. A question that asks about your brand by name almost always scores high, because the AI obviously talks about you when asked. Such prompts don't measure how AI engines discover you on their own, and they distort your averages. Keep your tracked prompts free of your brand name.

sections.heading: Competitors I've never heard of
sections.text: Unknown brands in AI answers are useful: they're the alternatives people see when you aren't cited. Add the most-mentioned ones to your competitors to track them properly.

sections.heading: An AI platform is missing
sections.text: Your plan sets which AI platforms your prompts are asked on. A self-hosted install runs every platform. On the cloud, some platforms come only with the higher plans.

sections.heading: Add more topics and prompts later
sections.text: You can add more at any time. On the **Topics** tab of the **Prompts** page, admins and managers add topics with **Add Topic** or from the **Topic Suggestions** card. **Prompt Suggestions** offers new prompts to track. New prompts run with the next daily run.

articles.title: Brand perception in AI answers

sections.text: The **Perception** tab of the Mentions & Sentiment page shows the words AI uses next to your brand, and how they compare with the words it uses for your competitors. The terms are taken from the sentences that name each brand by fixed rules, not by an AI model. A sentence that names two brands lends its words to both.

sections.heading: What AI associates with your brand
sections.text: The first card lists the words and phrases that appear next to your brand, ranked by the number of responses they appear in, each with its change from the previous period. Hover over a count to see its share of the responses naming you.

sections.heading: Brand shape and Brand × attribute
sections.text: **Brand shape: you vs top competitors** is a radar chart of your brand and your three most-mentioned competitors, on the attributes that tell them apart. It needs at least three attributes and at least one competitor named in the period. **Brand × attribute** shows the same attributes as a heat map: each attribute's share of the responses naming each brand, for you and up to four competitors.

sections.heading: Biggest gap
sections.text: Under the brand shape, **Biggest gap** names the attribute where one of the competitors on the brand shape leads you by the widest margin, when that margin is at least 20 points. For example, AI may use *affordable* in 45% of the responses naming a competitor but in only 10% of the responses naming you. A competitor's figures marked **Low sample** are left out, and the note doesn't show while yours are.

sections.heading: Frequently mentioned with
sections.text: This card lists the competitors named in the same responses as you, with the change from the previous period. It shows whether the set of brands AI considers alongside you is changing.

articles.title: Correct a wrong mention sentiment

sections.text: Every answer that names your brand is tagged Positive, Neutral or Negative toward your brand. If an answer's tone is tagged wrongly, you can correct it from the answer's side panel on the Mentions & Sentiment page, and every figure then counts it with the new sentiment.

sections.heading: Find and open the answer
sections.text: On the **Mentions** tab, the table's **Sentiment** filter or the **Most negative** sort helps you find the answers to check. Click a row to open the answer in a side panel. It shows the platform and model, the country, the date, the prompt with **View prompt**, the sentiment, your position and the topic. **Mention** shows the passage around your brand, **Also named in this answer** the competitors, **Full AI response** the answer as tracking stored it, and **Citations in this answer** each cited source.

sections.heading: Save a correction
sections.text: In the panel, click **Sentiment is wrong?**. Pick the new sentiment, add a note on why if you like, and click **Save correction**. From then on, every figure counts the answer with its new sentiment, and the original is kept in the history. The panel shows who made the correction, when, what the sentiment was before, and the note.

sections.heading: Who can correct a sentiment
sections.text: Only admins and managers can correct a sentiment. Other members can see past corrections in the panel, but not the **Sentiment is wrong?** button.

articles.title: How mention and sentiment figures are counted

sections.text: Each tracked answer that names your brand is tagged **Positive**, **Neutral** or **Negative** toward your brand. An answer that doesn't name you has no sentiment. Competitors have no sentiment yet, so every tone on the Mentions & Sentiment page is the tone toward your brand.

sections.heading: Total mentions and mentions
sections.text: **Total mentions** counts every time an answer names your brand, by its name or one of its domains: an answer that names you three times counts three. The platform table's Mentions column and the exported file count the same way. A mention in the **Mentions** table is different: it is an answer that names you at least once, so an answer naming you twice is still one mention. **Competitor framing** counts responses the same way.

sections.heading: Rates, sentiment and position
sections.text: **Mention rate** is the responses naming you divided by the tracked responses in the period. **Prompts with mentions** counts the prompts with at least one answer naming you, out of the prompts tracked. **Net sentiment** is the positive share minus the negative share of the responses naming you, from −100 to +100. Neutral answers count in the total. It is shown as a signed number such as +21, not as a percentage. **Position** is your brand's place among the brands an answer names, 1 meaning named first.

sections.heading: Low sample
sections.text: A figure that rests on fewer than 20 responses is marked **Low sample**. For the mention rate that means fewer than 20 tracked responses; for net sentiment, fewer than 20 responses naming you. A low-sample figure is shown without a change from the previous period, isn't tinted in the platform table, and is left out of **Biggest gap**. With so few answers, a single negative response moves the number a lot, so widen the date range or clear a filter before you draw conclusions from it.

articles.title: Mentions & Sentiment page

sections.text: The **Mentions & Sentiment** page, **Mentions** in the sidebar, shows where AI answers name your brand, in what tone, and next to which competitors. It reads the answers your tracking already stores, so opening it or changing a filter never asks an AI model again. It has three tabs: **Overview**, **Mentions** and **Perception**.

sections.heading: Filters
sections.text: All three tabs share one filter bar, for the brand active in the sidebar. **Date range** offers 24h, 7d, 30d (the default), 90d or Custom; a custom range is read as whole UTC days. **Platform** picks one AI platform or all of them. **Country** appears only when the brand tracks more than one country, and **Topic** only when it has topics. **Search** matches the prompts' text, also on the Perception tab, where the box reads *Search keywords…*. The tab and the filters are kept in the page's address, so a refresh or a shared link opens the same view.

sections.heading: Overview tab
sections.text: The **Overview** opens with a summary line: net sentiment and its change, the platform behind most of that change, and the competitors AI usually names next to you. Four cards follow: **Total mentions**, **Mention rate**, **Prompts with mentions**, and **Net sentiment** with its positive, neutral and negative split. **Mentions & sentiment over time** draws one point per day; the 24h view has no trend. **By AI platform** compares the platforms and notes when two platforms' net sentiment is 40 or more points apart. **Competitor framing** shows how often AI names each competitor and, under **Also names you**, how many of those answers name you too.

sections.heading: Changes from the previous period
sections.text: Every change compares the selected period with the period of the same length just before it. It is taken only on the prompts that were answered in both periods, so adding or pausing prompts doesn't show up as a rise or a fall.

sections.heading: Mentions tab
sections.text: The **Mentions** tab lists every answer that names your brand, 100 per page. Each row shows the prompt, the platform, the country when the brand tracks more than one, the **Mention context** around your brand, the **Sentiment**, the **Position** (#2 of 5 means named second of five brands), the **Co-mentioned** competitors, the topic and the date. The table's own controls filter by **Sentiment** and **Co-mentioned**, **Group by** prompt or platform, and **Sort** by Newest, Oldest, Most co-mentions or Most negative. Click a row to open the full answer in a side panel.

sections.heading: Copy summary and Export CSV
sections.text: The page header has three buttons. **Copy summary** copies the Overview as plain text: the filters, the summary line, the four figures and the period, ready to paste into a doc or a ticket. **Export CSV** downloads the answers that name your brand under the filters, one row per answer, up to 5,000 rows per file. From the Mentions tab, the file also follows the table's sentiment and co-mention filters and its sort. Lines above the rows record the filters, the period and the counts. **Reports** opens the Reports page.

articles.title: Act on mentions with the Action Center and content

sections.text: From the **Mentions** tab of the Mentions & Sentiment page, you can turn answers that name your brand into work: one Action Center action for a set of answers, or a content suggestion for an answer's prompt.

sections.heading: Send answers to the Action Center
sections.text: Tick the rows you want; the box in the table header selects every answer on the page. A bar appears with **Send to Action Center**, **Export** for a file of just the selected rows, and **Clear**. You can also send a single answer from its side panel. One send takes up to 100 answers, a full page. Sending the same answers again while their action is still open doesn't create a second one: the notification says **Already in the Action Center** and opens the existing one.

sections.heading: What the action contains
sections.text: The selected answers become one action, titled *Improve how AI describes you for "…"*, or *across N prompts* when they cover several. It quotes up to 10 of the answers with their platform, sentiment and excerpt. It is a **Protect** action when any of the answers is negative, and a **Growth** action otherwise; the larger the share of negative answers, the higher its impact. Its tasks walk you from inspecting the contexts you're mentioned in and analyzing the cited sources to strengthening how your brand is described, publishing, and measuring the outcome on the answers' prompts.

sections.heading: Suggest content
sections.text: **Suggest content** in an answer's side panel writes a content suggestion for the answer's prompt. When it is ready, the notification opens it in Content. If the prompt already has a suggestion, **Open existing** takes you there instead. Suggestions count toward your monthly content limit. Only admins and managers see **Suggest content**. A prompt can't get a suggestion until it has tracked answers and a prompt group; both arrive with its next tracking run.

articles.title: Add prompts to track

sections.text: A prompt is a question Ansvisor asks the AI engines for your brand every day, such as "best project management tool for agencies". Its answers show where your brand is named and cited. You can add prompts one at a time, many at once, or from suggestions. Admins and managers can add prompts.

sections.heading: Add a topic first
sections.text: Prompts are grouped under topics, so a brand needs at least one topic before it can have prompts. Without one, **Add prompt**, **Bulk import**, **Track** and suggestions say **Add a topic first**. Admins and managers get an **Add a topic** button that opens **Prompts › Topics** with **Add Topic**. Other roles are asked to have an admin or a manager add one.

sections.heading: Add one prompt
sections.text: On **Prompts › Tracked Prompts**, click **Add prompt**. On the **Single** tab, type the question and pick its topic, platforms and AI models. **Add to list** queues several, and **Save & close** or **Save & add more** saves them. It is tracked in the brand's location; add more later with **Track in more locations**.

sections.heading: Add many at once
sections.text: In the same dialog, open the **Bulk import** tab and upload a one-column Excel or CSV file of prompts. A preview marks each row **Valid**, **Duplicate**, **Error** or **Over plan limit**, and the valid rows that fit are imported. They get the platforms and models picked in the dialog and the brand's location. Set their topic afterwards from each prompt's **Edit**, and add locations with **Track in more locations**.

sections.heading: Add from suggestions
sections.text: Switch the list to **Prompt Suggestions**. Add one suggestion with its **+** button, or every listed one with **Add All**.

sections.heading: When the first results come
sections.text: A prompt has no results until it is first asked. **Add prompt** and **Bulk import** start right away when they can. A prompt added from suggestions, or one whose analysis couldn't start, gets its first results with the next daily run. Until then, for its first two days, its row says **Within 24h**.

sections.heading: What counts on your plan
sections.text: Every prompt counts on your plan's prompt limit, once in each location it is tracked in. Paused prompts don't count. If adding would pass the limit, Ansvisor adds the prompts that fit and says how many weren't added. Once the limit is reached, it adds nothing until you pause or remove prompts.

articles.title: How estimated AI search volume works

sections.text: AI assistants don't publish how often people ask them something, so every AI search volume in Ansvisor is an estimate. It is shown as a range, such as 540–2k, never as a single number. Totals, averages and a prompt's own page add a dashed **Estimate** badge; in tables the range alone marks an estimate.

sections.heading: How it's estimated
sections.text:
The estimate is the median monthly Google searches for the prompt's related keywords, times the share of Google searches that now get an AI answer (45% by default; a self-hosted server can change it).

When a prompt's volume is analyzed, Ansvisor picks five short Google keywords for its category and reads their monthly Google searches. Keywords Google has no data for are left out, and the median of the rest is the prompt's **Google Vol.** The Insights tab shows the AI share as **AI Adoption Rate**.

sections.heading: How the range is set
sections.text: The range is the AI share of the middle half of the keywords, kept within half to twice the estimate and at least 25% either side of it. With only one keyword to go by, the range is half to twice the estimate.

sections.heading: Confidence levels
sections.text:
- **High**: at least 3 of the prompt's keywords have Google search data, and the middle half of them are within 4× of each other.
- **Medium**: at least 2 have data, within 15× of each other.
- **Low**: anything else, including an estimate of 0.

Volumes fetched over six months ago count one level less; **Refresh Volumes** on the Insights tab gets newer ones.

sections.heading: Low-confidence estimates
sections.text: A low-confidence estimate is grey, its badge reads **Estimate · low confidence**, and it isn't used to rank on its own. **High Opportunity Prompts** leaves it out, and sorting **Tracked Prompts** by **Volume** puts it after the confident estimates, before prompts with no volume.

sections.heading: Read a range
sections.text:
Hover or focus a range or its badge to open the method note. It says how the estimate was built, how many of the related keywords have Google search data, the sources and their month, and the confidence with its date.

Measured numbers never carry the badge: your visibility, mentions and citations, Search Console clicks and impressions, or a suggestion's Analytics sessions. A range is always an estimate, with or without the badge; a single number without a range was counted, not estimated.

sections.heading: Totals, single keywords and AI guesses
sections.text:
Some estimates are built differently, and their note says so:

- **Totals and averages** (**Total Est. AI Volume**, **Avg. AI Volume**, and Similar Topics' **Est. AI Volume**): the sum of the lows to the sum of the highs; an average divides both by the prompt count. A total is high-confidence when at least 80% of its volume is, low when more than half is low-confidence, and medium otherwise. The note gives the mix.
- **One keyword** (each row of Similar Topics): only the AI share is assumed, so it is Medium with a ±25% range, or Low when it has no volume or is over six months old.
- **An AI's guess** (suggestions from Ansvisor Agents, the Brand Visibility page's Opportunities, and the Action Center's topic opportunities): always Low, from half to twice the guess. Track the prompt to get an estimate from its keywords' Google searches.

sections.heading: Compare prompts by their ranges
sections.text: Read volumes as ranges: compare prompts by their confidence as well as their size, and prefer high-confidence estimates when you decide what to work on first.

articles.title: Create content from a tracked prompt
synonyms: write a page for a prompt
start a draft from a prompt

sections.text: For admins and managers, each row in **Tracked Prompts** has a **…** menu with **Create content** and **Improve position…**. Use them to start a page written for the prompt, or to improve a page of yours that AI engines already cite.

sections.heading: Start a page with Create content
sections.text:
1. Click **Create content**. It opens **New content** at its Start step, titled with the prompt.
2. Pick a page type. Ansvisor picks one from the title; change it if it's wrong, now or later in the editor.
3. Choose **Who does it**: **Me** opens the Content Editor, **Agent** writes a draft for you to review, and **Team** sends it to the Action Center.
4. Check the overlap. Start reads your pages AI already cites for the prompt. If one already answers it, you can optimize that page instead of choosing **Create a new page**.

sections.heading: When a draft already exists
sections.text: If a draft that isn't published yet already covers the prompt, one started from the prompt, its topic or an opportunity, the menu shows **Open draft** instead. That way you don't start a second page for the same prompt.

sections.heading: The content step in Improve
sections.text:
**Improve position…** opens the prompt's positions panel. Its **Improve** tab starts with a content step, decided from the answers in the panel's period:

- No answer mentions or cites your brand: **Create content**, to start a new page.
- Your brand is named in under 20% of the answers, with 5 or more answers: **Optimize content**.
- Your average position is worse than #3, over 3 or more answers that name you: **Optimize content**.
- Anything else: no content step.

**Optimize content** opens Start on your page AI engines cite most for the prompt. When none is cited, Start lists your pages that answer the prompt so you can pick one. When a draft already covers the prompt, the step offers **Open draft**.

sections.heading: How Improve's suggestions are written
sections.text: The **Improve** tab's suggestions per platform are written from the answers' evidence and from this brand's last two Improve actions on the prompt for the same region: which of their suggestions were done or skipped, and how each platform moved since. They build on what moved, and don't suggest again what was done on a platform that didn't move, or what your team skipped. An action sent less than a week ago is too early to tell either way.

sections.heading: Suggestions that use competitor pages
sections.text: When the Action Center's **Compare competitor content and coverage** task has read pages cited for the prompt in the last four weeks, the **Improve** tab's suggestions also see what Site Audit's checks found on them: which checks each competitor page passes, and which they pass that your cited page doesn't.

articles.title: A prompt's own page and its real demand

sections.text: Click a prompt's text in **Tracked Prompts** to open its own page. It shows the prompt's visibility, mentions, citations and per-platform results. When the prompt has a volume, an **AI searches a month** card shows its estimate. Below the figures, **Demand · is this asked for real?** shows measured signals of whether people really ask it.

sections.heading: The four demand signals
sections.text:
Each signal shows its source and the day it was read:

- **Search Console**: impressions and clicks over the last 28 days for your Google queries that match the prompt, how many matched and the most seen one. Read every night.
- **Google Trends**: a 12-month line for the prompt's keyword, **Rising**, **Steady** or **Falling**, and the change on a year ago. Read about once a week.
- **People Also Ask**: the related questions Google shows for the keyword. Read about once a week.
- **YouTube**: the views across YouTube's top videos for the keyword, and the most viewed one. Read about once a week.

A query matches a prompt when at least half of its words are in the prompt, and counts for the closest prompt only.

sections.heading: When a signal is missing
sections.text:
Google Trends, People Also Ask and YouTube are read for the keyword with the most Google searches in the prompt's volume analysis, so the prompt needs its volume analyzed first. These weekly reads are off by default, and a self-hosted server can turn them on; until then their cards say **Weekly reads aren't turned on yet**. Search Console is read every night either way.

A card without its signal says why, for example **Connect Search Console to see real clicks** (with a **Connect Search Console** button for admins and managers), the first sync still running, or **Analyze volume first**.

sections.heading: Track a People Also Ask question
sections.text: Each People Also Ask question has a **+ Track** button for admins and managers. One click adds it as a tracked prompt in the prompt's topic, within your plan's prompt limit. A question your brand already tracks, even with different capitals, accents or punctuation, shows **Tracked** instead and isn't added twice.

sections.heading: Demand level
sections.text: The signals read come to a demand level, shown in the KPI row as **Demand · 3 of 4 signals** with the level, for example **High**. It carries a **Measured** badge, never **Estimate**.

sections.heading: How the demand level is scored
sections.text:
Each signal read gives 2 points when it's strong, 1 when there is some, 0 otherwise:

- **Search Console**: 1,000 impressions or more is strong, 100 or more is some.
- **Google Trends**: rising is strong, steady is some.
- **People Also Ask**: 4 questions or more is strong, 1 or more is some.
- **YouTube**: 100,000 views or more is strong, 5,000 or more is some.

The level is **High** at 60% of the possible points or more with at least two signals read, **Medium** at 30% or more, and **Low** below. A signal that was read and found nothing counts; one never read doesn't.

sections.heading: Demand and the Priority Score
sections.text:
The demand level feeds the Priority Score of the Action Center's actions about the prompt. **High** raises its demand to at least what about 2,500 monthly AI searches would give, and **Medium** to about 160. **Low** leaves it as it is, because signals that found little don't prove nobody asks.

When a prompt's level changes, the brand's open actions are scored again that night, and **Why this priority?** names a High or Medium level.

articles.title: Prompt Insights tab and volume analysis

sections.text: The **Insights** tab of the **Prompts** page shows the estimated AI search volume of your tracked prompts, their intent and the highest-demand prompts. It has no date range, because volume estimates aren't tied to a period.

sections.heading: Run a volume analysis
What the tab shows
sections.text:
For analyzed prompts you see:

- **Prompts Analyzed**, with how many keywords they cover, and **Total Est. AI Volume** and **Avg. AI Volume** across your prompts.
- Two **Prompt Volumes** cards: a chart of the total by answer engine, and a table with each prompt's **Google Vol.** and **Est. AI Vol.**
- Each prompt's **Intent**: Comparison, How-to, What is, Best / Top, vs. / Review, Recommendation, Problem Solving or Other.
- **High Opportunity Prompts**: the prompts with the most estimated AI searches. A low-confidence estimate isn't listed there on its own.
- **Similar Topics**: the most-searched keyword clusters across your prompts. **See all** opens its own page.
- **AI Adoption Rate**: the share of Google searches that get an AI answer, used in every estimate.

sections.heading: Where else estimated volumes show
sections.text:
- **Tracked Prompts**: the **Volume** column.
- A prompt's own page: an **AI searches a month** card, when the prompt has a volume.
- **Prompt Suggestions**: each AI suggestion's monthly range.
- Outside Prompts: the Action Center's affected prompts and topic opportunities, the Brand Visibility page's Opportunities, and a content opportunity's **Est. AI Volume**.

Exports mark estimated volumes, with their range and confidence, so a spreadsheet doesn't read them as counts.

articles.title: Track prompts in more locations

sections.text: A prompt can be tracked in several locations (countries, US states or cities), with its own figures in each one. In **Tracked Prompts** you compare them in the **Locations** view, and add or remove places with the **Track in more locations** dialog. Admins and managers add and remove locations.

sections.heading: The Locations view
sections.text:
The **Table | Locations** switch, above the table, opens **Locations**: one row per prompt and one column per location your prompts track, the most-tracked first (12 at most). Pick **Visibility**, **Position**, **Mentions** or **Citations**; cells are shaded light to dark, and for Position, named earlier is darker.

An **All prompts · average** row and a **Gap** column (the best location minus the worst) sit beside three cards: **Weakest location**, **Strongest location** and **Biggest gap between locations**. Click a cell to open the prompt's Positions panel for that location. The date range and filters work as in the table.

sections.heading: A location as a table column
sections.text: To see one location in the normal table, open **Columns** and use **Add a location column**. It adds a metric in one location, such as Visibility in one country, as its own column, up to eight of them.

sections.heading: Add locations
sections.text:
Open **Track in more locations** from **+ Add location** in the Locations view, **+ Track** in a cell, or **Locations › Add locations** in the bar that shows when you select prompts. Then:

1. Pick one or more countries, US states or cities. A country one engine doesn't answer from says so, and that engine is skipped there while the others run.
2. Choose the prompts: the one you clicked, the selected ones, a topic, or every prompt shown.
3. Check **Plan usage**. Every prompt in every location counts once on your plan's prompt locations. Paused prompts don't count.

sections.heading: When locations would pass your plan's limit
sections.text: If the choice would pass your plan's limit, the dialog says how many it needs and how many are left, and saves nothing. Pick fewer prompts or places, or follow your plan's way to track more.

sections.heading: Which engines answer from a state or city
sections.text:
**US states** are asked by every engine from the state itself. Google's engines asked a state country-wide until October 2026, so their answers from before then stay in the country's column.

**Cities** are asked only by the engines that can answer from a city: Google AI Mode, Google AI Overview and the API models (OpenAI, Claude). ChatGPT, Perplexity, Copilot, Gemini and Grok answer per country, so they skip a city and their answers stay in the country's column; track the country too to see them. A city column says **AI Mode · AIO · APIs**. A city counts as one location on your plan, like a country.

sections.heading: What a new location shows
sections.text:
A location you just added has no answers until the next daily run asks it. Until then, its cells say:

- **Within 24h**: it's tracked there, and the first results come with the next daily run. While a new brand's first tracking runs, **Arriving now**: that tracking is asking it.
- **Paused**: the prompt is paused, so it isn't asked anywhere until you resume it.
- **No engine here**: none of the prompt's engines answers from that place. Add an engine that does, or remove the location.

When your plan's prompt locations are used up, **+ Track** reads **Limit reached**. It still opens the dialog, which shows your plan's way to track more.

sections.heading: Stop tracking in a location
What happens to past results
sections.text: Past results stay. The prompt is no longer asked there from the next daily run, and the answers already collected there aren't deleted. The dialog shows how many tracked locations it removes and how many it frees on your plan; a paused prompt's locations go too, but free nothing. When no prompt shown is tracked in a location any more, its column leaves the Locations view.

articles.title: Prompt Suggestions and Add All

sections.text: **Prompt Suggestions** gives you new prompts to track. Open it with the switch above the filters on the **Prompts** tab of the **Prompts** page. Each refresh writes up to 25 prompt ideas, each with a topic label and a one-line reason.

sections.heading: Where suggestions come from
sections.text:
Suggestions come from four sources. The sources filter (**All sources**) shows one of them, **From your data** for both Google sources, or **Ansvisor Agents only**:

- **Ansvisor Agents**: written by AI from your brand and tracking data. Each shows an estimated monthly AI volume as a grey range.
- **Google Search Console**: queries people already search, with their impressions over the last 28 days.
- **Google Analytics (GA4)**: pages that earn revenue or conversions, or already get AI visits, with that evidence on the row.
- **Your catalog**: for an online shop with a product catalog, the questions a shopper asks before buying in its categories, using their price bands. Hover the badge for the category; the **Shopping** filter lists them.

When Search Console or Analytics is connected, a share of each refresh is drawn from their data.

sections.heading: A brand without topics
sections.text: Suggestions are written for a brand's topics. If the brand has none, **Generate Suggestions** and **New** ask you to add a topic first and open **Prompts › Topics**, without using any AI.

sections.heading: Add, dismiss or refresh suggestions
sections.text:
Use **Search prompts…** to narrow the list, **+** to add a suggestion, **×** to dismiss it and **New** to generate a fresh list. **Clear All** asks first, then dismisses every suggestion listed. Admins and managers can add and generate suggestions; analysts can also dismiss them. Those from Search Console or Analytics stay hidden for 30 days once dismissed.

Suggestions expire after 48 hours. Click **New** for fresh ideas, for example after you change your content.

A prompt added from suggestions gets its first results with the next daily run.

sections.heading: Add every suggestion at once
sections.text: **Add All** adds every suggestion listed to **Tracked Prompts**, and the added ones leave the list. Like **Clear All**, it acts on what's listed, so a source filter or a search narrows it. Each prompt passes the same plan check as a single **+**.

sections.heading: When your prompt limit stops Add All
sections.text:
When your plan's prompt limit stops **Add All** partway, an amber note above the list says how many suggestions couldn't be added and how many were added before the limit.

To add the rest, upgrade your plan or ask us to raise your limit, as the note says, or pause as many prompts as the note names and try again. **Go to Tracked Prompts** opens the list where you can pause prompts.

sections.heading: How AI suggestions are written
sections.text:
The suggestion engine considers five signals:

1. Your brand's name, description and language.
2. Your tracked prompts, so it doesn't repeat them.
3. Your topics, so it reuses their labels when relevant.
4. The competitors named most in your recent tracked AI answers.
5. The estimated volumes of your tracked prompts, so its own estimates stay in proportion.

articles.title: Query Fan-outs behind AI answers

sections.text: Behind an answer, an AI engine can run searches of its own. The **Query Fan-out** tab of the **Prompts** page lists the searches the AI engines ran behind their answers to your tracked prompts. In the sidebar, the **Prompts** item opens it as **Query Fan-outs**.

sections.heading: Which engines share their searches
sections.text: Copilot and Perplexity share the searches behind their answers. ChatGPT's are sampled on some days, and the ChatGPT API shares them when it searches. Google AI Overviews, AI Mode, Gemini and the Claude and Gemini API models don't share them: their chips say **not shared**, and a note under the chips names them.

sections.heading: Engines
sections.text:
Above the list, **All engines** counts the searches found in the range, and each engine that answered has a chip of its own. A chip gives the share of that engine's answers that came with searches, such as "40% of answers", and how many searches it ran. Click a chip to see only that engine's searches; click it again, or **All engines**, to see them all.

An engine that usually shares its searches but sent none is marked in amber, "none since" a date, with a note under the chips. Its answers are still tracked as usual; only the list of searches is missing. A **not shared** chip is faded and doesn't filter.

sections.heading: By prompt
High frequency
Track a search as a prompt
sections.text: Admins and managers can click **+** on a search to track it as a prompt of its own and measure your visibility on it. The row then reads **Tracked**, which opens the new prompt. A brand without topics is asked to add one first.

sections.heading: Pick the date range
sections.text: The tab uses the **Prompts** page's date range: 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d or custom. It opens on 7d, because one day of answers holds few searches; a range you picked on another tab carries over. The tab has no **Location** filter: it shows the searches from every location you track.

articles.title: Topics tab for prompts grouped by theme

sections.text:
**Topics** is a tab of the **Prompts** page. It groups your tracked prompts by theme, so you can see how your brand does in AI answers at a higher level than single prompts.

The tab uses the page's date range (24h, 7d, 30d, 90d or custom) and opens on the last 24 hours. It has no Location selector, because topics aren't split by location.

sections.heading: The cards at the top
sections.text:
Four cards sum up your topics:

- **Tracked topics**: how many topics you have, and how many prompts have no topic yet.
- **Best performer**: the topic with the highest Visibility score.
- **Biggest gap**: the topic with the lowest score, among those above 0.
- **Top mover**: the topic whose score rose most, in points; when every topic fell, the one that fell least.

sections.heading: The Topic leaderboard
The buttons beside the tabs
sections.text:
- **Add Topic** creates a new, empty topic.
- **Export CSV** downloads the leaderboard as a CSV file.
- **Manage topics** opens the brand's topic settings.

sections.heading: A topic's page
Topic Suggestions
sections.text:
The **Topic Suggestions** card on the Topics tab starts folded, and remembers whether you left it open. Open it to see AI-generated topic ideas for your brand. Topics you already track and ideas you dismissed don't come back.

Admins and managers can **Refresh** for new ideas, add an idea to your topics, or dismiss it. A new topic starts empty: assign prompts to it to start tracking it.

sections.heading: Add and rename topics
sections.text:
Only admins and managers can change topics; other roles can view them.

- **Add Topic** creates a new, empty topic.
- To rename a topic, click **Manage topics** and use the pencil icon beside it in the brand's topic settings. Its prompts stay attached.

Keep topic names short (two to four words) and intent-driven: "Pricing" works better than a long descriptive phrase.

sections.heading: Delete a topic
sections.text:
Admins and managers open the **…** menu at the end of a topic's row and choose **Delete topic**. The dialog says how many prompts are in the topic.

The prompts aren't deleted: they keep their tracking and results, and move to prompts without a topic. After you confirm, **Undo** puts the topic back for 10 seconds.

sections.heading: Use topics for planning
sections.text:
- **Editorial planning**: pick the topic with the lowest score and the weakest competitor lead; it's a good candidate for your next content sprint.
- **Reporting**: topic-level stories, such as which themes you own and which you're losing, are easier to share than prompt-level metrics.
- **Spotting drift**: a topic that drops while others stay flat usually signals one competitor's surge or content that has aged.

articles.title: Tracked Prompts list, statuses and columns

sections.text: **Tracked Prompts** lists every prompt Ansvisor asks the AI engines for your brand, with its results over the date range you pick (24h, 7d, 30d, 90d or custom). It sits on the **Prompts** tab of the **Prompts** page: a switch above the filters picks **Tracked Prompts** or **Prompt Suggestions**. A range you pick carries over to Topics and Query Fan-out.

sections.heading: Prompt statuses
sections.text:
Each row has a status:

- **New** (amber): added in the last 24 hours. New prompts lead the table until you sort by a column; after a day they read as Active.
- **Active**: tracked on its schedule.
- **Paused**: kept, but not tracked.

The table opens on **Active + New**. The **Status** filter, or the cards under **Plan & usage** (click **Show**), show one status or all of them.

sections.heading: Rows without figures
sections.text: A new prompt has no results until it's first asked. Until then, for its first two days, the row says **Within 24h** in its first figure column, such as Visibility. While a new brand's first tracking runs, it says **Arriving now** instead: that tracking is asking it. A paused prompt says **Paused** there when the Status column is hidden. An older prompt with no results in the range, such as days without a run, shows a dash, as does a range that ended before today.

sections.heading: Choose your columns
sections.text:
**Columns**, beside the search box, picks the table's columns: tick one to show or hide it, and drag it, or use its arrows, to move it. **Prompt** always shows. The **Added** column shows when each prompt was added; click it to sort by it. The **Volume** column shows each prompt's estimated AI search volume. The **Work** column, with its filter, shows your content work on each prompt: **To do**, **In progress**, **Done** or no status.

Your columns are saved for you on this brand. Admins and managers can tick **Share with everyone on** the brand to make theirs the brand's view; everyone can still change their own, or go back with **Reset to the brand's view**.

sections.heading: Share a column view with the brand
sections.text: Admins and managers can tick **Share with everyone on** the brand: their columns become the brand's view, which everyone without columns of their own sees. Anyone can still change their own. **Reset to the brand's view** goes back to the brand's columns, and **Reset to default** to the default columns when the brand has none.

sections.heading: Filter by performance
sections.text:
The **Performance** filter groups prompts by where your brand is named in their AI answers over the selected range, across every platform the prompt tracks:

- **Best**: named in the first third of the brands an answer lists.
- **Good**: named in the middle third.
- **Late**: named in the last third.
- **Missing**: named in fewer than half the answers.

Late and Missing list the furthest behind first. A prompt with no answers in the range, such as a new one, has no performance yet. The **Positions** column shows your average position and its change; hover it for each platform, or use its chart button to open the positions panel.

sections.heading: Open a prompt or act on it
sections.text:
Click a prompt's text to open its own page, with its visibility, mentions, citations and per-platform results. For admins and managers, each row's **…** menu offers **Edit**, **Pause tracking** (or **Resume tracking**), **Improve position…**, **Suggest content** (or **Open content suggestion**), **Create content** (or **Open draft**) and **Delete**.

**Export CSV** downloads the list. Estimated volumes in it are marked as estimates, with their confidence and range, so a spreadsheet doesn't read them as counts.

articles.title: Daily Pulse email digest

sections.text: The Daily Pulse is a short digest for each brand that goes out after its scheduled tracking run. It shows the headline numbers for the period, then lists what went well (highlights) and what needs attention (warnings). It comes by email on Ansvisor Cloud, and can also go to your webhook, on cloud and self-hosted alike.

sections.heading: Choose how often it comes
sections.text:
Open **Settings › Notifications**. Every active brand has its own row with a frequency and a recipient list. Admins and managers can change them; other members see them read-only. The **Manage notification settings** link at the bottom of every pulse email opens this page.

- **Daily** (the default): after every scheduled daily tracking run.
- **Weekly**: once a week on Monday (UTC), covering the last 7 days compared with the 7 days before.
- **Only when notable**: like Daily, but skipped when there are no highlights and no warnings.
- **Off**: no email and no webhook.

sections.heading: Choose who gets it
sections.text: Enter email addresses separated by commas. Leave the field empty to send to every member of the organization. Each address is checked when you save: if one isn't valid, the save is rejected and the invalid entries are listed under the field, so fix or remove them and save again. Up to 50 addresses are stored. Recipients apply to the email only, not to the webhook.

sections.heading: AI Traffic weekly digest
sections.text: Each brand's row also has **AI Traffic weekly digest**: every Monday, last week's AI visits in one summary line, with the top three changes. It goes to the same recipients, and isn't sent while the Daily Pulse is **Off**.

sections.heading: When it is sent
sections.text: A pulse follows a brand's scheduled daily tracking run; manual runs and single-prompt refreshes never trigger one. It waits up to 90 minutes for late answers, so its numbers match the dashboard. No pulse is sent when the frequency is **Off**, or **Weekly** and it isn't Monday; when the brand already had one that day; when there are no tracking results in the window; when the frequency is **Only when notable** and nothing is notable; or, on the cloud, when the subscription isn't active or trialing.

sections.heading: What's in a pulse
sections.text: The KPIs are **Visibility**, the **7-day trend**, **Mentions** and **Citations**, **Positive sentiment**, and **Prompts you appear in**. For Daily and Only when notable, the period is the latest completed tracking run, at most 24 hours, compared with the run before it. For Weekly, it is the last 7 days compared with the 7 days before. The email subject carries the visibility score and the weekly trend; on Weekly, it says Weekly Pulse.

sections.heading: Highlights
sections.text:
- **First citation**: a URL from a prompt's Target URLs list was cited by an AI engine for the first time. Up to 5 are listed.
- **Prompt gain**: a prompt's visibility score rose by 5 points or more this week versus last week. The top 3 are listed.
- **Competitor overtaken**: last week a competitor's score was at or above yours; this week yours is higher.
- **New engine**: your brand was mentioned or cited on an AI platform for the first time ever.

sections.heading: Warnings
sections.text:
- **Sharp drop**: your visibility score fell week over week by at least 3 points and at least 30% of last week's score, for brands with 10 or more tracked prompts.
- **Competitor surge**: a competitor's score rose by 15 points or more week over week.
- **Competitor crossed**: a competitor at or below your score last week is above it this week.
- **Lost citations**: a prompt with an estimated AI volume above zero was cited on at least 60% of its result days in the last 14 days, then not at all on its 3 most recent.

A smaller fall shows as **Visibility slipping**, in the email and the webhook alike.

sections.heading: Repeats and collection problems
sections.text: The same warning about the same subject, such as a surge by the same competitor, isn't repeated within 7 days. Highlights have no such pause. If an AI platform's result volume collapses on Ansvisor's side, the pulse treats it as a collection problem rather than a real change: **Sharp drop**, **Visibility slipping** and **Lost citations** are held back, and the email notes which platforms were affected.

sections.heading: Send it to a webhook
sections.text: Every pulse also goes to the brand's active webhook, if it is subscribed to the Daily Pulse event: under **Content**, open **Webhook Settings** and tick **Daily Pulse created**. On self-hosted installs, this is the only way the pulse is delivered. The webhook carries the same KPIs, highlights and warnings as the email. The frequency applies to it too; the recipient list doesn't.

articles.title: Connect Looker Studio

sections.text: The Ansvisor connector for Looker Studio pulls your AI visibility metrics into Looker Studio. One dashboard can then show AI visibility next to organic traffic, such as GA4 sessions and Search Console clicks, on one date axis. For now, the connector is shared by link: ask Ansvisor for the current one.

sections.heading: Connect
sections.text:
1. In **Settings › MCP & API Keys**, click **New key**, give it a name and click **Create**. Copy the key now: it is shown only once.
2. Open the connector's link. Looker Studio asks you to authorize the connector, then asks for a key: paste the one you copied.
3. Pick the brand and a metric set, then click **Connect** and **Add to report**.

sections.heading: Metric sets
sections.text:
Each data source gives one metric set; add several data sources to use more than one in a report.

- **Visibility Trend (daily)**: by date, the average visibility score, mentions, citations, tracked results and the competitor average.
- **Share of Voice by Platform**: by platform, brand mentions, competitor mentions and share of voice.
